events.text: {npc} has found the carp kite you flew as a child, torn and folded in a chest, and has spent a month mending it with new paper. It is crooked. {He} is very proud of it.

choices.text: Fly it at once, in the yard

effects.log: It climbs, wobbles and holds. {npc} holds the string for a while, saying nothing, which is the most {he} ever says.

choices.text: Hang it on the wall of your room

mem.note: hung my kite on the wall

effects.log: It hangs over your bed, crooked and red. {npc} straightens it every time {he} passes.

events.text: A strong spring wind, and {npc} turns up with the carp kite under one arm and a spool of new silk string under the other. {He} says the string was cheap. It was not.

choices.text: Take it to the hill together

mem.note: went up the hill with me

effects.log: Half the village children follow you up. The kite goes higher than the old pine. {npc} pretends the wind did it.

choices.text: Teach the neighbour's children to fly it

mem.note: taught the children with my kite

effects.log: Six children, one kite, much shouting. {npc} referees and is unfair to everyone equally.

events.text: {npc} is too stiff now for the hill, but asks if you still have the kite. You do. {He} would like to see it fly once more, from the doorstep.

choices.text: Fly it from the yard while {npc} watches

mem.note: flew it for me from the step

effects.log: It goes up over the roof. {npc} laughs out loud, a young laugh, and you will remember it all your life.

choices.text: Give the kite to {npc} to keep

effects.log: {npc} hangs it by {his} own bed. Visitors are told the whole story, with improvements.

events.text: {npc} has knitted you a pair of socks so thick you cannot get your boots on over them. {He} watches you try.

choices.text: Wear them, and buy bigger boots

effects.log: You walk like a duck for a winter, and your feet are never once cold.

mem.note: wore my socks by the stove

effects.log: You live in them by the stove. {npc} counts this as a victory.

events.text: Another winter, another pair. These are thinner, after complaints. They have a pattern of little red plum flowers that you suspect took a month.

effects.log: {npc} says {he} did not do them for you, {he} did them for the plum tree, and blushes.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to teach you the stitch

effects.log: Your first sock is a sort of bag. {npc} keeps it, and shows it to people.

events.text: The winter {npc} cannot knit any more: the fingers are too stiff. {He} hands you a basket of red wool and asks you to finish the last pair.

choices.text: Finish the pair, plum flowers and all

effects.log: They are lumpy and the flowers look like beans. {npc} wears them every day until spring.

choices.text: Take the wool to the best knitter in the street

effects.log: The knitter does it beautifully and asks who taught you to care about socks. You tell them.

events.text: You once lent {npc} your savings to buy a plough ox. Today {npc} leads the ox to your gate, tied with a red ribbon, and says it is half yours, in law, by {his} own reckoning.

effects.log: Half an ox, it turns out, is a lot of arguing about which half eats.

choices.text: Say the ox is all {npc}'s, and the debt is paid

effects.log: {npc} weeps a little into the ox's neck. The ox bears it.

events.text: {npc}'s ox has had a calf, and {npc} has named it after you. The calf is brown, stubborn and eats laundry.

effects.log: The calf eats your sleeve. {npc} says it is a sign of family feeling.

choices.text: Help {npc} build a pen for it

effects.log: A good pen. The calf is out of it by evening. {npc} is delighted with the calf's spirit.

events.text: The calf named after you is grown and pulls the best plough in the village. At the harvest feast {npc} stands up and toasts the ox, and you, in that order.

choices.text: Stand and bow to the ox

mem.note: bowed to the ox at the feast

effects.log: The whole feast laughs. The ox, tied outside, lows at the right moment. It is talked about for years.
You say the ox had a good teacher. {npc} is too pleased to finish {his} cup.

events.text: {npc} has kept a clay pot of rice in the corner of the storeroom since the year you were born, adding a handful every month you were away, and has decided today the pot is full.

choices.text: Cook it all for a feast

effects.log: The whole lane eats from it. {npc} says every grain is a month you came back alive.

choices.text: Keep the pot as it is

effects.log: The pot stays in the corner. You find yourself adding handfuls to it, too.

events.text: {npc} has started a second pot. This one, {npc} explains, is for the months you stay home. It fills more slowly.

effects.log: A whole season of meals at the same table. The second pot fills to a third. {npc} is unbearable about it.

choices.text: Add a handful from the road every month

effects.log: Rice from twelve provinces, in one pot. {npc} can tell them apart, or says so.

events.text: Two pots in the storeroom, both full. {npc} asks you to choose which one to cook for the New Year.

effects.log: It tastes of twelve provinces. {npc} says it tastes of worry, and eats three bowls.

choices.text: The pot of months at home

effects.log: {npc} cooks it slowly, the way it was filled. You eat it in the kitchen, the two of you.

events.text: {npc} has tied a new tassel to your sword: long, silk and a shocking shade of pink. It was, {he} explains, the only colour the shop had that was not boring.

effects.log: The tassel becomes known. Opponents remember it. Some of them remember little else.
{npc} brings back a tassel of deep blue, and keeps the pink one on {his} own belt, out of spite.

events.text: At a tournament, an opponent mocks the pink tassel, and {npc}, in the crowd, stands up and shouts that it was a gift. The whole stand turns to look.

ok.log: You win cleanly. The pink tassel flies. The crowd chants something about it, roughly.

fail.log: You lose, and bow to {npc} anyway. The crowd applauds the bow more than the winner.

effects.log: The opponent laughs too. After the match the two of you share noodles, and {npc} explains the tassel at length.

events.text: {npc} has had a child, and the child, the first time it sees your sword, reaches for the faded pink tassel and will not let go.

choices.text: Give the tassel to the child

effects.log: It hangs over the cradle. {npc} says the child will grow up with terrible taste and a brave heart.

choices.text: Tie a new tassel for the child

mem.note: tied a tassel for my child

effects.log: You buy the pinkest one the market has. {npc} says you have learned nothing, and is delighted.

events.text: {npc} presses a small tin of tea into your hands: the good tea, saved for thirty years for an occasion that never came. {He} has decided you are the occasion.

mem.note: drank the good tea with me

effects.log: It is old, and it is wonderful. {npc} tells you the story of the year {he} bought it, which involves a goat.

choices.text: Save it for a better day

mem.note: kept my tea for a better day

effects.log: {npc} laughs and says that is what {he} said thirty years ago.

events.text: {npc} wants to know how you are getting on with the tea. Truthfully: there is one cup left, and you have been afraid to drink it.

effects.log: You split it in two cups so small they are thimbles. {npc} says the second half is always the best.

choices.text: Buy a new tin of the same tea (4 taels)

effects.log: The tea house has never heard of it. You find it in the fourth shop. {npc} pretends it tastes the same.

events.text: The tin is empty, and {npc} keeps asking for it back, to keep buttons in. {He} has a lot of buttons.

effects.log: You find buttons in every corner of the house. {npc} sorts them by colour all afternoon and is perfectly happy.

choices.text: Fill it with tea again, quietly

effects.log: {npc} opens it expecting buttons, smells it, and has to sit down for a moment.

events.text: {npc} gives you a box tied with string: every letter you ever sent home, kept in order, with the bad spelling corrected in red ink.

effects.log: You were a very strange young person. {npc} kept every word of it.
{npc} says {he} could not help it. Also, you still spell plum wrong.

events.text: {npc} has started writing you letters in return, though you live two streets away. They are delivered by a neighbour's child for a sweet.

effects.log: The neighbour's child grows rich in sweets. The letters are about the weather, the cat and you.
{npc} is pleased, and then gives you that day's letter anyway, because it was already written.

events.text: The box of letters has two halves now, yours and {npc}'s, and {npc} wants to know which half you would save in a fire.

effects.log: {npc} says that is the right answer and the wrong reason, and will not explain.

choices.text: {npc}'s, for the weather and the cat

effects.log: {npc} says nothing at all for a while, and then corrects your spelling of cat.

events.text: Years ago you held a ladder for {npc} through a whole storm while {he} fixed the roof. {npc} has never forgotten. Today {he} has built you a ladder of your own, of good elm.

choices.text: Use it at once on your own roof

effects.log: The ladder is perfect. Your roof was fine. You fix it anyway.

choices.text: Hang it on the wall as a decoration

mem.note: hung my ladder on the wall

effects.log: {npc} visits, sees it on the wall, and does not know whether to be flattered.

events.text: Another storm, and {npc}'s roof again. This time it is you on the ladder and {npc} holding it, shouting advice into the wind.

choices.text: Fix the roof, ignoring the advice

ok.log: The roof holds. {npc} says it is because of the advice.

fail.log: You slide off the last tile into the water butt. The roof holds anyway. {npc} cannot stop laughing.

mem.note: listened to me on the ladder

effects.log: The advice is good. The roof is better than new. {npc} is unbearable for a week.

events.text: {npc} is too old for ladders now, and makes you promise never to go up one without someone holding it.

effects.log: You keep it. Mostly. {npc} somehow always knows when you do not.

choices.text: Make {npc} the official holder of all ladders

effects.log: {npc} takes the post seriously. No one in the lane goes up a ladder without being inspected.

events.text: {npc} has made you a pair of cloth shoes with soles of thirty layers, stitched so tight they could stop a knife. {He} hides them in the rafters so you will find them the day you leave home.

effects.log: Three provinces, and the soles are still good. Your feet think of {npc} every step.

choices.text: Leave them in the rafters, for best

effects.log: {npc} is not sure whether to be pleased. You are keeping them for a good day.

events.text: A letter from {npc}: how are the shoes? There is a drawing of a shoe, in case you have forgotten what they look like.

effects.log: {npc} hangs the soles over the stove as a trophy. A new pair is on the way within the month.

choices.text: Send a drawing of the shoes on the road

mem.note: drew my shoes on the road

effects.log: Your drawing is worse than {npc}'s. {npc} says so, warmly, in the next letter.

events.text: You find {npc} at home making a pair of shoes so small they fit in one hand. They are, {he} says, for whichever child in the family needs them first.

effects.log: Your stitches are crooked. {npc} leaves them in, so the child will have something of yours.

choices.text: Buy a bolt of good cloth for more (3 taels)

effects.log: There will be shoes for every child in the family for ten years. {npc} plans them all aloud.

events.text: {npc} gives you a copper coin with a square hole, worn smooth, on a red string. It is, {he} says, the first coin {he} ever earned, and it has never once been spent.

effects.log: It sits against your chest through good years and bad. You never once spend it either.

choices.text: Ask what it was earned for

effects.log: Carrying a bride's chair across a river, aged ten, it turns out. {npc} tells it like a war story.

events.text: You come home broke, and {npc} looks at the coin round your neck and asks if you were tempted.

effects.log: {npc} laughs and says {he} was tempted every week for sixty years. That is what the coin is for.
{npc} looks at you a long time and says you are a terrible liar, and gives you dinner.

events.text: {npc} asks for the coin back, for one day, to show an old friend who was there at the river.

effects.log: It comes back that evening with a second string, from the old friend, who wants it known they carried the other pole.

choices.text: Go with {npc} to see the friend

mem.note: came with me to see the friend

effects.log: Two old people argue for two hours about which of them did the most carrying. You have never laughed so much.

events.text: {npc} never had a coin to repay you for the year you paid {his} school fees. Today {he} arrives with a basket of sesame cakes, made with {his} own hands, enough for a month on the road.

choices.text: Take them all, and say the debt is paid

effects.log: They are slightly burnt and perfect. You eat the last one in a strange province and feel at home.

choices.text: Share them out on the street

effects.log: The whole street eats sesame cakes. Three people ask {npc} for the recipe.

events.text: {npc} has opened a small stall selling sesame cakes. The sign over it says, in big letters, the name of the stall. It is your name.

mem.note: asked me to change the sign

effects.log: {npc} refuses. The cakes are named after you. People order a dozen of you every morning.

choices.text: Buy the first dozen of the day (1 tael)

effects.log: {npc} refuses your coin, then takes it, then puts it on a shelf to keep.

events.text: The stall is a shop now, with two ovens and an apprentice. {npc} wants you to come and taste a new cake, which has a secret in the middle.

choices.text: Taste it and guess the secret

ok.log: Plum jam. {npc} is furious you guessed. The apprentice is delighted.

fail.log: You guess wrong three times. It was plum jam. {npc} is so pleased you could not tell.

mem.note: ate four of my new cakes

effects.log: {npc} takes the silence as the highest praise, which it is.

events.text: You once carried {npc} to a herbalist two valleys away in the snow. {npc} has spent the years since learning herbs, and has brought you a packet of everything you might ever need, labelled.

effects.log: Forty herbs, forty labels in tiny writing. You learn which one is for bruises and which is for liars.
A long, smelly, happy month. You come out of it knowing which root is which, mostly.

events.text: A fever is going round the lane, and {npc} is going door to door with {his} herb basket. {He} wants you to carry it.

mem.note: carried my basket through the fever

effects.log: A hard week. Every house in the lane is well by the end of it. You catch the fever and {npc} cures you, very smugly.

choices.text: Pay for more herbs from the market (3 taels)

effects.log: The market herbalist is surprised by the order. {npc} complains about their quality, and uses them all.

events.text: {npc} has written the herb knowledge down at last, in a little book, and asks you to keep it.

effects.log: It is in your pack from then on. You use it twice in a bad year and it works both times.

choices.text: Copy it for the lane's children

mem.note: copied my book for the children

effects.log: Six copies, six children. {npc} tests them all on the labels, sternly.

events.text: {npc} has had a blacksmith make you a kitchen knife, of the same steel as a sword. It is, {npc} says, for when you finally learn to cook.

mem.note: learned to cook with my knife

effects.log: Your first meal is bad. Your tenth is good. {npc} eats the first one anyway, bravely.

choices.text: Keep it sharp and use it for everything

effects.log: It cuts rope, bread and once, a bandit's bowstring. {npc} says that is not cooking.

events.text: {npc} comes to dinner, at your house, for the first time. {He} brings no food at all, on purpose.

choices.text: Cook the best meal you can

ok.log: The fish is good. The rice is good. {npc} asks for seconds and does not comment, which is the highest praise.

fail.log: The fish is a disaster. {npc} eats it all and tells you it was exactly like {his} own first fish.

effects.log: You get it almost right. {npc} can tell what you got wrong, and loves you for the rest.

events.text: {npc} cannot cook any more, hands too shaky, and comes to you for dinner twice a week. {He} still criticises the salt.

effects.log: {npc} salts everything far too much. You eat it and say nothing. It is the best dinner of the week.

choices.text: Teach {npc} the dish you got right

effects.log: You hold the knife, {npc} gives the orders. It is exactly like your first lesson, the other way round.

events.text: {npc} has made a quilt out of every robe you ever outgrew. There is your first red jacket in the middle and a burnt sleeve in one corner from that time with the stove.

effects.log: You sleep twelve hours. It smells of the old chest and of {npc}.

choices.text: Find the story of every patch

effects.log: It takes all evening. {npc} remembers every robe and what you did in it. Some of it is embarrassing.

events.text: {npc} has started a second quilt, from robes the rest of the family outgrew, and needs one patch from you: something you wear now.

mem.note: gave a robe for the quilt

effects.log: Your sleeve is in the middle of the new quilt, between your cousins. {npc} says that is where it belongs.

mem.note: gave the sash for the quilt

effects.log: The sash runs across the quilt like a river. {npc} says it is the best patch and the most difficult to sew.

events.text: {npc} asks you, quietly, who should have the two quilts after {him}.

choices.text: Say {npc} should keep them both a long time yet

effects.log: {npc} says that is not an answer. You say it is the only one you have. {He} lets it go.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to decide and write it down

effects.log: {npc} writes it out. The list is long, fair and has notes. You are told nothing of what it says.

events.text: {npc} has carved you an oar of mountain ash, because, {npc} says, everyone in the family needs a spare oar, and you never had one.

choices.text: Take it to the river at once

effects.log: The oar is heavy and true. You row up the river and back. {npc} times you.

choices.text: Ask why everyone needs a spare oar

effects.log: A long story about a flood and a cousin and one oar. It ends happily, mainly because of the spare.

events.text: The river is in flood. {npc} sends a child running: is the spare oar still dry?

mem.note: brought the oar in the flood

ok.log: You wade the last part. The boat's own oar has broken. Yours gets everyone across.

mem.note: brought the oar in the flood

fail.log: You fall twice, but get the oar there. {npc} hauls you into the boat like a fish.

choices.text: Lend it to the ferry instead

mem.note: lent the oar to the ferry

effects.log: The ferry gets thirty people across with it. {npc} says that is exactly why everyone needs one.

events.text: {npc} has carved a third oar, smaller, and wants you to give it to the youngest in the family who can row.

choices.text: Teach the child to row with it

mem.note: taught the child with my oar

effects.log: The child rows in circles for an afternoon and then, suddenly, in a straight line. {npc} watches from the bank.
Yours is uglier. {npc} says it will float, which is the main thing.

events.arc: The Name in the Temple Book
events.text: {npc} has paid the temple to write your name in its book of blessings, in gold, at the top of a page. {He} takes you to see it.

effects.log: Your name in gold, in a book of names. A monk says your page is very popular with moths. It is a joke, probably.

choices.text: Ask to write {npc}'s name under yours

effects.log: The monk allows it for a small donation. {npc} tries to argue, and loses.

events.arc: The Name in the Temple Book
events.text: A fire in the temple. The monks are carrying out the books. {npc} is at the gate, wanting to know if the book of blessings is safe.

ok.log: You carry out twelve books, the book of blessings last. {npc} turns to your page right there in the street.

fail.log: Smoke and heat. You get out four books. One of them is the right one.

mem.note: kept me back from the fire

effects.log: The monks save the book. {npc} is very cross with you for holding on, and grateful later.

events.arc: The Name in the Temple Book
events.text: The temple's new book of blessings has been copied out, and the monk asks you whose name should go first on your page this time.

effects.log: {npc} reads it and says nothing, and then tells everyone in the lane, separately.
The monk says it is not usual. It is done anyway. The moths will have to share.

events.text: When {npc} married, you paid for the roof. Now {npc}'s family has had a good harvest and arrives at your house with a cart of fired tiles, to replace your leaking thatch.

choices.text: Accept, and all hands on the roof

effects.log: Three days, eleven relatives and a roof that does not leak. You have never been so dry.

choices.text: Accept, and give half to a neighbour

effects.log: The widow next door has a dry roof too. {npc} pretends that was the plan all along.

events.text: A typhoon. Your new tiles hold. {npc}'s old roof, two streets away, does not.

effects.log: A full house for a week, children on every mat. Nobody remembers it as a bad week.

choices.text: Climb on {npc}'s roof in the storm

mem.note: held my roof in the storm

ok.log: You tie down the worst of it with rope. The rest of the roof survives the night.

fail.log: The wind is too strong. You come down soaked. The family comes to your house anyway.

events.text: {npc}'s family repaired the roof with tiles of the same kiln as yours, and invites you to the dinner to celebrate it, which is under the roof, in case anyone doubts it.

effects.log: It is a very bad speech, mostly about the colour of kilns. The family loves it.

choices.text: Bring a dish of your own

effects.log: You bring braised pork. It is eaten under the new roof in eleven minutes.

events.text: {npc} has made you a bamboo mouth harp, the kind {he} played as a herd boy. It makes a noise like a frog thinking.

effects.log: A month of frog noises. Then, suddenly, a tune. {npc} claps along.
{npc} plays the herd song from the mountains. Halfway through {he} stops, because {he} has forgotten the end. You never learn the end.

events.text: {npc} wants a duet: two mouth harps, at the harvest supper, in front of everyone.

ok.log: You play together, slightly apart. The supper roars for more.

fail.log: You lose the tune at once. {npc} keeps going alone, loudly, and the supper claps for you both.

effects.log: You keep the beat on an upturned pot. {npc} plays better than {he} has in years.

events.text: {npc} has remembered the end of the herd song at last, in the middle of the night, and wakes the house to play it to you.

choices.text: Learn the end there and then

mem.note: learned the end of the song

effects.log: It is a short end, just three notes. {npc} plays them over and over until the dog howls along.

choices.text: Write it down so it is never lost

effects.log: You write it the way scholars write music. {npc} cannot read it but keeps the paper in {his} sleeve.

events.text: The year of the bad harvest, you sent {npc} your rice. {npc} has never been able to repay rice with rice, so {he} sends a jar of salted plums every spring, very sour, with a note that says: still not enough.

choices.text: Eat them with rice and write back

effects.log: Your mouth puckers until dinner. You write back that it is enough.

choices.text: Share them with the whole street

effects.log: The street winces as one. Three people ask for the recipe.

events.text: The plum jar arrives, and also {npc}, in person, with a second jar for a neighbour who was kind to {him} once and is now ill.

mem.note: came with me to the neighbour

effects.log: The neighbour eats one plum and laughs for the first time in a month. {npc} counts that.

choices.text: Find a doctor for the neighbour (2 taels)

effects.log: You paid 2 taels for a doctor. The doctor says the plums will do no harm and may do good.

events.text: {npc} has taught you the plum recipe at last, and this spring you are expected to make the jar yourself and send it to {npc}.

effects.log: Your plums could strip paint. {npc} writes back: perfect. Still not enough.
{npc} writes back: these are not salt plums, they are a cake. Still not enough.

events.text: {npc} has given you the writing desk {he} studied at as a young person, for the exams {he} never passed. It has a burn mark and a carved character on the inside of the drawer.

effects.log: You study better at it. You do not know why. The burn mark is comforting.
It is the character for patience. {npc} carved it the night {he} failed the third time.

events.text: You find a second carved character in the drawer, very small, that {npc} never mentioned. It is a name, and not one you know.

effects.log: A friend from the exam hall, {npc} says, who passed, and stopped writing. {npc} still thinks of them.

ok.log: A retired magistrate in the next county. The two of them meet and argue about a poem from forty years ago.

fail.log: The trail goes cold. {npc} says it is enough that you looked.

events.text: {npc} asks you to carve a third character in the desk, for whatever you have learned at it.

effects.log: Your carving is clumsy. {npc} runs a thumb over it for a long time.
{npc} says it is the right one, and that {he} wishes {he} had thought of it.

events.text: {npc} gives you {his} best laying hen, a speckled thing with opinions. It is, {npc} says, the most valuable thing {he} owns. The hen does not like you.

ok.log: A week of grain and patience. The hen sits on your foot. You are accepted.

fail.log: The hen pecks you twice. {npc} says that is affection, from a hen.

choices.text: Keep the hen at {npc}'s house, and visit

effects.log: You visit the hen weekly. You visit {npc} weekly. {npc} sees through it at once and is pleased.

events.text: The speckled hen has hatched eleven chicks, and {npc} says they are all yours, by right, as the hen's owner.

choices.text: Take half and give half back

effects.log: Five and a half chicks each, by the hen's reckoning. The sixth one chooses {npc}.
{npc}'s yard is full of speckled chicks, and {npc} is busy and happy and complains about them all day.

events.text: {npc}'s yard is a speckled flock now, and {npc} has decided to give one hen to every child in the lane, and wants you to choose which hen goes to which child.

effects.log: The bossiest hen goes to the shyest child. It works. {npc} calls you a matchmaker of hens.
Chaos, feathers and joy. Every child gets a hen and every hen gets a name. {npc} writes them all down.

events.text: {npc} shakes you awake before dawn: the fish come up to the lantern on moonless nights, and tonight there is no moon.

effects.log: Three fish, one eel and a great deal of silence. {npc} says it is the best night of the year.

choices.text: Say you will go next time

effects.log: {npc} goes alone. In the morning there is a fish on your pillow, which is a message.

events.text: The moonless night again, and {npc} has made you a lantern of your own. It is shaped like a fish, so the fish will trust it.

choices.text: Fish all night by the fish lantern

effects.log: The fish do seem to trust it. You catch more than {npc}, which is not forgiven.

mem.note: talked all night in the boat

effects.log: You catch nothing. You learn more about {npc} than in twenty years. The lantern burns down.

events.text: {npc}'s eyes are bad now in the dark, and {he} asks you to row and hold the lantern, just this once.

mem.note: rowed for me in the dark

effects.log: {npc} talks to the fish the whole night, and catches two, by feel.

choices.text: Bring a young cousin to learn

effects.log: Three of you in the boat now. The child falls in once. {npc} says that is the first lesson.

events.text: {npc} is making dumplings for the whole family and says you may help on one condition: every dumpling you make is counted, and you will be judged.

effects.log: Twenty-four dumplings, judged neat but unadventurous. {npc} is pleased in a judging sort of way.
A fish, a hat, a dragon. The dragon bursts in the pot. {npc} laughs until {he} cries.

events.text: The New Year dumplings again, and {npc} has hidden a copper coin in one of them, as {he} does every year. This year {npc} hints that it is in one of yours.

effects.log: Nineteen dumplings. The coin is in the nineteenth. {npc} had put it in the first.

choices.text: Let a younger cousin find it

mem.note: let the cousin find the coin

effects.log: You steer the right dumpling to the smallest cousin. {npc} sees, and says nothing, and pinches your cheek.

events.text: {npc} sits at the side this year, hands in {his} lap, and lets you make the dumplings and do the counting and the judging.

effects.log: The cousins are outraged. {npc} says you have learned everything.

mem.note: put the coin in my bowl

effects.log: {npc} bites the coin and pretends to be surprised, badly, and keeps it on the shrine all year.

events.text: {npc} has found a way up onto the roof by the woodpile, and wants to show you the stars from up there, where the eaves do not get in the way.

mem.note: climbed on the roof with me

effects.log: You lie on the warm tiles. {npc} names the stars, mostly wrongly. It does not matter.

choices.text: Hold the ladder and listen from below

effects.log: {npc} shouts the names of stars down to you. The neighbours shout back to be quiet.

events.text: {npc} has made a chart of the stars from the roof, every one named, by {npc}, with names like Big Noodle and The Dog's Eye.

effects.log: You never learn the proper names. To you the bright one in the east is The Dog's Eye for life.

choices.text: Copy the proper names beside them

effects.log: Half the chart is scholar's names, half is {npc}'s. {npc} says {his} are better, and they are.

events.text: Grown and both busy, you have not been on the roof together in years. Tonight {npc} is at the woodpile, looking up.

effects.log: The tiles creak more. The stars are the same. The Dog's Eye is still there.
{npc} reads it by lantern and laughs at the Big Noodle, and then points it out, still there.

events.text: {npc} is carving a lion into the gatepost, very slowly, a little each day, and asks for a second pair of hands. It is, {he} says, a guardian for the house. It looks like a dog with a cold.

effects.log: Your mane is wilder than {npc}'s face. The lion looks surprised now. It is an improvement.
{npc} knows it is not. {He} is pleased anyway, and carves more slowly, to make it last.

events.text: A thief tried the gate last night, saw the lion and ran. {npc} is beside {him}self with pride.

effects.log: The lion's reputation spreads. Children leave it sweets. {npc} eats them.

choices.text: Point out the dog next door

effects.log: {npc} says the dog and the lion work together. You cannot argue with that.

events.text: {npc} wants a second lion for the other gatepost, and the hands are too stiff now. {He} holds the chisel out to you.

ok.log: Your lion is better. You make it look slightly like the first, so they match. {npc} sees.

fail.log: Your lion looks like a cat with a grudge. {npc} says the house now has two kinds of guardian.

choices.text: Carve it together, your hands and {npc}'s eye

effects.log: {npc} tells you every cut. It takes all summer. The two lions face each other like old friends.

events.text: {npc} has a rice terrace at the very top of the hill that nobody else will farm, and needs help planting it. The water comes down from a spring, and you can see three villages from it.

mem.note: planted the top terrace with me

effects.log: Mud to the knee and a view to the sea. {npc} sings planting songs, all of them rude.
The spring water runs straight for the first time in years. {npc} watches it all afternoon.

events.text: Harvest on the top terrace. {npc} says the rice from up there tastes of the sky. It tastes of rice. Good rice.

effects.log: A hundred trips. Your legs are iron. {npc} cooks the first pot on the terrace itself, on a fire of stalks.

choices.text: Bag a little for every house in the village

effects.log: Every house gets a little sky rice. Every house says it tastes of rice, and thanks {npc} anyway.

events.text: {npc} cannot climb to the top terrace any more, and wants you to have it.

effects.log: You climb up every spring. You bring {npc} the first bowl. It tastes of the sky.

choices.text: Plant a plum tree there for {npc}

mem.note: planted a tree on the terrace

effects.log: The plum flowers the next spring. {npc} can see it from the gate, white on the hill.

events.text: {npc} has cut puppets out of oiled paper, a general, a dragon and a very fat official, and puts on a play behind a lamp and a sheet for you alone.

effects.log: The general wins, gloriously. The dragon eats the official. You ask for it again.
Your dragon has stage fright and falls off the stick. {npc} makes it part of the story.

events.text: {npc} wants to put on the shadow play for the whole lane at the Lantern Festival, and you are to do the voices.

effects.log: The fat official's voice becomes famous. The real official, who was there, laughs loudest.

choices.text: Do the sound of the thunder

effects.log: You beat a tin tray behind the sheet. The children scream happily. {npc} is very pleased with the thunder.

events.text: {npc}'s puppets are faded and torn, and {npc} wants to cut new ones, and wants you to choose the new story.

effects.log: The new puppet of {npc} is a hero of the lane, with a ladle. {npc} protests and keeps it on the shelf.
The general, the dragon and the fat official, all new. The lane cheers the same places it always did.

events.text: {npc} goes to the well every dawn before anyone is up. Today {he} asks you to come, and carry the second bucket.

effects.log: The lane at dawn is grey and quiet. {npc} talks more there than at home.
You win and spill half. {npc} wins with a full bucket. You learn something.

events.text: The well rope has frayed, and {npc} has been talking about it for a month. Nobody has done anything.

effects.log: Hemp and patience. The rope you make lasts eleven years. {npc} tells everyone who made it.

choices.text: Buy one at the market (1 tael)

effects.log: A good rope. {npc} says it is too good for this well, and is pleased.

events.text: At dawn there are two figures at the well again, but this time it is you carrying both buckets, and {npc} walking beside you with nothing.

effects.log: {npc} talks the whole way, about the lane when {he} was young. The sun comes up on the third story.

choices.text: Ask what {npc} used to think about, alone at dawn

effects.log: {npc} says: you. Then picks up a bucket anyway.

events.text: {npc} asks you to sit with {him} while {he} works, and sings: songs from the village {he} came from, which is gone now, under a reservoir. Nobody else in the house knows the words.

effects.log: A song about a red ox and a stubborn girl. {npc} makes you sing it back seven times.
{npc} draws it in the dust: the well, the temple, the house. All under water now, {he} says. Still there.

events.text: {npc} wants to write the village songs down before they are lost, and cannot write. You can.

effects.log: Forty-one songs. Some are rude. {npc} insists every word goes in.

choices.text: Get a scholar to do it properly (3 taels)

effects.log: The scholar is moved and writes a preface. {npc} cannot read it, and has it read aloud twice.

events.text: On the bank of the reservoir, where the drowned village lies, {npc} wants to sing the songs one last time to the water.

mem.note: sang to the village with me

effects.log: Forty-one songs to the water. A fisherman stops rowing to listen. At the end {npc} is lighter.

choices.text: Row {npc} out over the old temple

effects.log: You find the spot by {npc}'s memory. {npc} sings the temple song straight down into the water.

events.text: {npc} and a neighbour have been rivals in braised pork for twenty years. Today is the yearly tasting, and {npc} wants you to judge.

effects.log: The neighbour's is better, this year. {npc} does not speak to you for a day and then asks what was wrong with the pork.

choices.text: Find something to praise in both

effects.log: You call it a draw. Both cooks are furious. Both invite you to dinner next week, separately.

events.text: {npc} has a new secret ingredient, and has been testing it on you every day for a week. You are very full.

ok.log: A little orange peel. {npc} is horrified you could tell, and also proud.

fail.log: You never guess. {npc} will not tell. It was orange peel.

effects.log: Star anise. {npc} scoffs, tries it, and wins the tasting.

events.text: The neighbour has fallen ill, and the tasting is off this year. {npc} is cooking two pots anyway.

choices.text: Carry one to the neighbour with {npc}

mem.note: came to the neighbour with me

effects.log: The neighbour eats it and says it is the best {npc} ever made. {npc} cries in the kitchen.

choices.text: Cook the neighbour's recipe for them

effects.log: {npc} knows the neighbour's recipe exactly, it turns out. Twenty years of tasting.

events.text: {npc} is mending fishing nets on the jetty and asks you to hold the wooden needle. {npc}'s fingers move like a weaver's. Yours move like a crab's.

effects.log: One good knot by sunset. {npc} ties a bell to it so you can always find it.
Every hole has a story. A pike, a storm, a cousin's elbow. {npc} tells them all.

events.text: A huge fish has torn a hole in {npc}'s best net, the size of a door. {npc} says only two people can mend it in a day.

effects.log: A whole day, side by side. Your knots are good now. {npc} does not check them, which is the compliment.

ok.log: You and the fish fight for an hour. You win. The village eats it. The net is mended by {npc}, grinning.

fail.log: The fish wins. You come back wet. {npc} has mended the net already, and laughs.

events.text: {npc} has made a small net, perfect, and asks you to hang it in your own house, for luck.

effects.log: The net hangs over the door. Any guest who comes through is told it catches bad luck. Nobody argues.
It catches three small fish. You bring them to {npc}, who says they are the luckiest fish in the river.

events.text: On the night of a bad argument at home, {npc} finds you on the roof of the old granary, where you used to hide as children.

effects.log: You say nothing for an hour. Then {npc} makes a joke about the argument, and it is over.
You talk until the moon is down. {npc} takes your side completely, which is not fair, and is exactly right.

events.text: The granary is to be pulled down. {npc} wants to spend one last night on its roof.

choices.text: Bring food and stay till dawn

mem.note: stayed till dawn on the granary

effects.log: Cold dumplings and old jokes. At dawn you carve your names in the ridge beam.

choices.text: Take a tile from the roof to keep

mem.note: took a tile from the granary

effects.log: Two tiles, one each. {npc} keeps {his} on the windowsill for the rest of {his} life.

events.text: Where the granary stood there is a new house now. {npc} has come by to complain about it, as you both do every year.

effects.log: The new house is too tall, too neat and has no good roof. You agree on everything.

choices.text: Knock and ask to see the roof

mem.note: got us onto the new roof

ok.log: The family laughs and lets you up. It is not as good a roof. It will do.

fail.log: The family does not let you up. You walk home talking about how they will regret it.

events.text: {npc} does slow exercises in the courtyard every dawn, an old man's set from an old master. Today {he} beckons you to stand beside {him}.

effects.log: The moves are slow and surprisingly hard. By the end your legs shake and {npc} is not even breathing.
A wandering monk, {npc} says, who taught {him} the set for a bowl of rice and never came back.

events.text: {npc} has decided you are ready for the last move of the set, which nobody else in the family was ever taught.

effects.log: It is a turn of the hand, nothing more, and suddenly the whole set makes sense. {npc} looks very pleased.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to teach it to the whole family

mem.note: shared the move with the family

effects.log: The courtyard is full at dawn now. {npc} grumbles about the noise and is happier than ever.

events.text: {npc} is too unsteady now for the set, and sits on the step at dawn and watches you do it.

effects.log: You do it as slowly as {npc} did. {npc} corrects your left foot. It was wrong for twenty years.

choices.text: Teach it to a child while {npc} watches

effects.log: The child is terrible. {npc} gives notes from the step. It is the best dawn of the year.

events.text: {npc} has picked the persimmons and wants them laid out on the roof to dry, every one turned to the sun. There are four hundred.

effects.log: Neat rows. {npc} inspects from below and moves three.

choices.text: Lay them out in the shape of a dragon

effects.log: The neighbours come out to look. {npc} pretends to be cross and tells everyone you did it.

events.text: Birds have found the persimmons on the roof. {npc} is waving a broom from the yard and wants you up there.

effects.log: You lose eleven persimmons and gain respect for crows. {npc} brings you lunch on the roof.

choices.text: Make a scarecrow of {npc}'s old robe

mem.note: made a scarecrow of my robe

effects.log: The crows are terrified of it. So, a little, is {npc}.

events.text: The persimmons are dry and sweet, and {npc} wants you to choose who in the family gets the first string.

mem.note: gave the first to the youngest

effects.log: The youngest eats the whole string. {npc} says that is the correct result.

mem.note: gave the first string to me

effects.log: {npc} protests, eats one and hangs the rest in {his} room where {he} can see them.

events.text: {npc} is going up the hill to gather wild greens and wants you to carry the basket and learn which leaves are which.

effects.log: Six good leaves and one that would make you sick for a week. {npc} makes you say them back.
You learn no leaves at all. You learn that {npc} once wanted to be a boatman.

events.text: Spring on the hill. {npc} wants to test you: you gather, {npc} inspects.

ok.log: A full basket, no bad leaves. {npc} cooks it that night and calls it your soup.

fail.log: One bad leaf. {npc} finds it at once and laughs, and teaches it again.

choices.text: Find the place {npc} found as a child

effects.log: A hollow full of wild garlic, exactly where {npc} said. {npc} sits down in it.

events.text: {npc}'s knees will not take the hill. You go up alone, and bring the basket back.

choices.text: Bring back the greens and the news of the hill

effects.log: You describe every tree. {npc} corrects you on two of them, from memory.

choices.text: Bring back a pot of hill earth for the yard

effects.log: You plant the wild garlic in the yard. It grows. {npc} visits it every morning.

events.text: {npc} is painting characters on the whitewashed wall with water and a big brush. They dry and vanish in a minute. {He} says that is the point.

effects.log: Your characters vanish faster, being thinner. {npc} says yours are honest.
{npc} says if nothing stays, you can try again forever. You do not understand, and then you do.

events.text: {npc} has a real sheet of paper and real ink, and wants you to write one character, the best you can, to keep.

effects.log: It is not bad. {npc} hangs it in the kitchen, where the steam will slowly fade it.
{npc} looks at it a long time and says the third stroke is wrong, and keeps it anyway.

events.text: The wall again. {npc} hands you the big brush and stands back to watch.

choices.text: Write a whole poem in water

mem.note: wrote a poem on the wall

effects.log: It vanishes line by line as you write. {npc} reads every line before it goes.

choices.text: Write one character and let it dry

effects.log: The character for together. It vanishes. {npc} says it was the best you ever did.

events.text: On a cold night {npc} asks you to sit up with {him} by the brazier, and tells you about the fox that lives behind the temple and borrows people's shoes.

effects.log: The fox once borrowed a magistrate's shoes and gave judgments in them for a week. You laugh until bedtime.
{npc} says every word, then winks, then says every word again more firmly.

events.text: A pair of shoes has gone missing from the temple steps. The village says it was the fox. {npc} says nothing, very loudly.

choices.text: Go and look behind the temple

effects.log: You find the shoes in a hollow tree. And fox prints. {npc} is beyond happy.
{npc} gives you a look of perfect innocence. The shoes reappear the next morning, polished.

events.text: {npc} asks you, now you are grown, to tell {him} a fox story for once.

effects.log: The fox takes up cultivation and fails, because it keeps eating its pills. {npc} laughs and corrects nothing.
You get it almost right. {npc} fixes the ending, which is better.

events.text: {npc} pulls noodles by hand at the family stall: one lump of dough, stretched and folded until it is a hundred threads. Today {he} is short of hands, and offers you the dough.

ok.log: Your noodles are thick as rope, but they are noodles. {npc} cooks them.

fail.log: The dough falls on the floor in one piece. {npc} picks it up and starts again, laughing.

effects.log: You see the turn of the wrist at the end. {npc} sees you see it.

events.text: {npc}'s wrist is sore and the stall has a line of customers. {npc} looks at you.

choices.text: Pull the noodles for the line

ok.log: Uneven, thick, but enough. The customers do not complain. {npc} supervises with one hand.

fail.log: A disaster of dough. The customers eat rice instead. {npc} says you will be a noodle cook yet.

choices.text: Take the money and send the line round the corner

effects.log: You run the line while {npc} pulls slowly. Nobody leaves.

events.text: {npc} has given up the stall and asks if you want the dough box, the board and the secret.

effects.log: The secret is a pinch of something you are sworn never to say. You never do.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to give them to the apprentice

mem.note: gave my stall to the apprentice

effects.log: The apprentice weeps. {npc} pretends it was {his} own idea, which by evening it is.

events.text: Your birthday, and {npc} has made the longevity noodle: one single noodle, as long as the table is wide, many times over. You must eat it without biting it through.

ok.log: Slurped in one piece. {npc} claps. A long life is guaranteed, says {npc}, no refunds.

fail.log: It breaks. {npc} makes another one, at once, and stands over you.

choices.text: Share it with {npc} from both ends

effects.log: You meet in the middle and both laugh too hard to finish. {npc} says that counts.

events.text: {npc}'s birthday, this time. You decide to make the noodle yourself.

ok.log: It is lumpy but it is one piece. {npc} eats it slowly, and does not break it.

fail.log: It is in four pieces. {npc} eats them in order and says that is four long lives.

choices.text: Buy the best noodle in town (1 tael)

effects.log: It is very long and very good. {npc} says it is not as good as the one you would have made.

events.text: {npc} is too busy with a household of {his} own to make the noodle now, but still comes every year to watch you eat one.

choices.text: Eat it slowly, in front of {npc}

effects.log: {npc} counts under {his} breath. You do not break it. {npc} looks very satisfied.
You eat together from two bowls. Neither breaks. {npc} says that settles it, you will both live forever.

events.text: {npc}'s best goat has climbed a cliff behind the village and will not come down. {npc} wants you to fetch it, because, {he} says, you climb like a goat yourself.

ok.log: You reach the goat. The goat walks down past you. You climb down after it.

fail.log: You slip and slide down on your back. The goat comes down to look at you, and so is caught.

effects.log: A handful of salt on a rock. The goat is down in a minute. {npc} says that is cheating and gives you supper.

events.text: The goat is on the cliff again, and this time it has a kid with it.

mem.note: brought down the goat and kid

ok.log: You carry the kid down inside your coat. The mother follows, bleating at you.

fail.log: The kid you get. The mother goat comes down alone, in its own time.

choices.text: Build a fence at the foot of the cliff

effects.log: The fence holds for a month. Then the goats find the gap. {npc} says the fence was a nice thought.

events.text: {npc} has decided the cliff goat is too clever to keep, and wants to give it to you.

effects.log: The goat climbs your roof on the first day. You become famous in your street.

choices.text: Find it a home with the temple

effects.log: The monks love it. It climbs the bell tower. The bell rings at odd hours, and the monks call it a sign.

events.text: {npc}'s child is to sit the county exam, and is terrified, and {npc} asks if you could spend some evenings helping with the essays.

effects.log: Twenty evenings of essays on virtue. The child improves. So, unexpectedly, do you.

choices.text: Teach the child to stop being afraid instead

effects.log: You take the child for long walks and tell them how much you failed. It works better than the essays.

events.text: The results are posted. {npc} cannot bear to look, and sends you to read the list.

ok.log: The child's name, near the top. You run all the way back. {npc} drops a pot.

fail.log: Not this year. You walk back slowly. {npc} and the child are already planning next year.

choices.text: Take the child to read it together

effects.log: Whatever the list says, you are both there. That is what {npc} wanted.

events.text: {npc}'s child has a post now, a small one, in another county, and sends {npc} a letter thanking you, which {npc} reads aloud at every meal.

effects.log: Your letter is about virtue, as a joke. The child writes back an essay, also as a joke. {npc} keeps both.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to stop reading it aloud

effects.log: {npc} stops for exactly one meal.

events.text: {npc} is marrying off a child and is worried about one thing: a certain relative, who sings at weddings, loudly, for hours. {npc} wants you to manage it.

choices.text: Keep the relative busy all evening

effects.log: You talk to the relative about fishing for four hours. Nobody sings. You know everything about fishing.

choices.text: Let the singing happen, and join in

effects.log: Two of you sing, which is worse, and also, somehow, the best part of the wedding.

events.text: The relative who sings has heard what you did at the wedding and wants to take you fishing, as a friend now. {npc} finds this hilarious.

effects.log: The relative does not sing. The relative talks. You catch eight fish.
Three of you in a boat. The relative sings. {npc} pushes the relative in. Everyone is happy.

events.text: The relative who sings has died, and {npc} asks if you will sing at the funeral, since you are the only one who knows the songs.

mem.note: sang the songs at the funeral

effects.log: Loudly, for hours. Nobody stops you. {npc} sings the chorus.

choices.text: Sing one song, the fishing one

effects.log: You sing it once, quietly. {npc} says that was the right one.

events.text: {npc}'s well has gone sour, and {npc} is going to dig a new one by hand, and asks if you will take turns in the hole.

effects.log: Twelve days in a hole, passing up baskets of earth. At twenty feet: water, cold and sweet.

choices.text: Hire two diggers to help (3 taels)

effects.log: Done in four days. {npc} insists on paying you back in pickled vegetables, for a year.

events.text: The new well's water is the best in the lane, and the neighbours want to use it. {npc} asks what you think.

effects.log: The lane comes with buckets. {npc} becomes the most important person in the street.

choices.text: Share it, but ask for help with the upkeep

effects.log: Every house gives one day a year. The well is kept perfectly. {npc} keeps a ledger of the days.

events.text: A dry summer, and {npc}'s well is the only one in the district still giving water. There is a queue round the block at dawn.

choices.text: Help {npc} keep order at the well

effects.log: A long summer. Everyone gets water, the old first. {npc} says you two dug the best thing either of you ever made.

choices.text: Dig a second well beside it

ok.log: Twenty feet down, the same cold water. The district is saved. Your name is on a stone by the well.

fail.log: Dry at thirty feet. You fill it in. {npc} brings you tea in the hole.

events.arc: The Ox Is Off Its Feed
events.text: {npc}'s ox will not eat and stands with its head down, and {npc} is frightened: the planting is in a week.

choices.text: Sit with the ox through the night

effects.log: At midnight the ox lies down. At dawn it eats. {npc} says it needed company, like everyone.
A stone in its hoof. The horse doctor takes it out, laughs at {npc}, and is paid in rice cakes.

events.arc: The Ox Is Off Its Feed
events.text: Planting week. The ox is well, but {npc} has hurt {his} back, and cannot hold the plough.

ok.log: Crooked rows, but rows. The rice does not mind. {npc} supervises from a chair on the bank.

fail.log: The ox and you disagree. The ox wins. {npc}, from the chair, sends you clear instructions.

choices.text: Bring two neighbours to share the work

effects.log: Three people, one ox, one day. The field is planted. {npc} feeds everyone.

events.arc: The Ox Is Off Its Feed
events.text: The old ox is too old to work. {npc} cannot bring {him}self to sell it.

choices.text: Let it graze out its life on your land

effects.log: The old ox stands under your tree for four years. {npc} visits it more than you.

choices.text: Help {npc} buy a young one, and keep both (3 taels)

mem.note: helped me buy a young ox

effects.log: You paid 3 taels. The old ox teaches the young one everything, mostly bad habits.

events.text: {npc}'s thatch is thin, and the rains are coming, and {npc} would rather die than ask the neighbours. So {he} asks you.

effects.log: Your thatch is not beautiful. It keeps out the rain. {npc} says the rain has given up.

choices.text: Pay a thatcher, and help (2 taels)

effects.log: The thatcher teaches you the trick of it. {npc} gives the thatcher tea and you a lecture on spending.

events.text: The rains, and a leak right over {npc}'s bed. {npc} has moved the bed and not told anyone.

choices.text: Climb up in the rain and fix it

mem.note: fixed the leak in the rain

ok.log: Soaked to the bone, but the leak is stopped. {npc} dries you by the stove like a child.

fail.log: You fall off the ladder into a puddle. The leak is half fixed. {npc} calls it a fine effort.

choices.text: Bring {npc} to your house until the rain stops

mem.note: took me in for the rains

effects.log: Two weeks of {npc} rearranging your kitchen. You find things in it for years.

events.text: {npc} has been saving coppers for a tile roof for ten years, and has almost enough, and wants your help choosing the tiles.

effects.log: Plain, strong and grey. {npc} says they are sensible, which is the highest praise.

choices.text: Choose green glazed ones and make up the difference (3 taels)

effects.log: The only green roof in the lane. {npc} pretends to be embarrassed and sits under it every evening.

events.text: A matchmaker has been calling on {npc} about a cousin, and {npc} does not like the match, and cannot say no to the matchmaker, who is formidable. {npc} wants you to be there.

choices.text: Be there and say no politely

effects.log: The matchmaker leaves smiling, somehow. The cousin is free. {npc} treats you to dinner.

choices.text: Ask the cousin what they want

effects.log: The cousin wants to marry someone else entirely, a carpenter. {npc} did not know. Everything changes.

events.text: The cousin and the carpenter want to marry, and {npc} is not sure about the carpenter, and wants you to inspect.

ok.log: Beautiful joints. Honest prices. You report favourably. {npc} gives in.

fail.log: You cannot tell good joints from bad. You say so. {npc} decides anyway, and decides yes.

effects.log: The carpenter is patient, kind, and catches nothing. {npc} accepts the match.

events.text: The cousin and the carpenter have a child, and the carpenter has made {npc} a chair, and {npc} wants you to sit in it to see if it is as good as people say.

effects.log: It is perfect. {npc} does not let anyone else sit in it, ever.

choices.text: Ask the carpenter to make another for you (3 taels)

effects.log: You have a chair like {npc}'s. Now you both sit in your chairs and compare them.

events.text: {npc} has dropped {his} ring in the duck pond while washing, and cannot get it, and the ducks are no help at all.

choices.text: Wade in and feel for it

ok.log: An hour in the mud. Your hand closes on it. {npc} washes it, and you, at the well.

fail.log: No ring, many leeches. The ring turns up a week later in a duck.

effects.log: A day of buckets. The ring is in the middle. The ducks are furious.

events.text: {npc} tells you what the ring is: the only thing {he} has from {his} own mother, who died young.

effects.log: {npc} talks for an hour, about a laughing woman who could whistle. You never knew any of it.

choices.text: Promise the ring will stay in the family

effects.log: {npc} nods and wears it on a string after that, safe from ponds.

events.text: {npc} puts the ring in your hand and closes your fingers over it.

effects.log: It is a little loose. You wear it on a string too. You never go near ponds.

choices.text: Keep it for the next in the family

mem.note: kept the ring for the next

effects.log: You wrap it in red silk. {npc} says the laughing woman would have liked you.

events.text: Rats in {npc}'s granary, and {npc} has declared war, and wants you as a general.

effects.log: The cat is lazy. It eats one rat and sleeps on the rice. The rats respect it anyway.
Forty holes. The rats find a forty-first. {npc} calls it a draw.

events.text: The rats have taken the granary roof. {npc} has a plan, involving a drum, a bell and you on the roof at night.

effects.log: The drum, the bell, you, {npc} shouting orders, every neighbour awake. The rats leave in disgust. So do the neighbours.

ok.log: Store the rice in clay jars. The rats starve out. {npc} says {his} plan would have worked too.

fail.log: Your plan fails. {npc}'s plan is tried next. It fails louder.

events.text: {npc} has made peace with the rats, apparently. {He} leaves a little rice out for them, and they leave the rest alone.

effects.log: {npc} says that every war ends in a treaty, and the rats keep theirs better than most kings.

choices.text: Help write the treaty on the granary wall

effects.log: You write it in big characters. The rats cannot read. {npc} says they understand the spirit.

events.arc: The Chess Under the Locust Tree
events.text: {npc} plays chess under the locust tree in the square every afternoon, and beats everyone, and is looking for someone new. {He} pats the stone stool opposite.

ok.log: You lose, but late. {npc} says you are the first in a month to make {him} think.

fail.log: You lose in nine moves. {npc} sets up the board again at once.

effects.log: You watch {npc} demolish a retired general. You learn more than from any book.

events.arc: The Chess Under the Locust Tree
events.text: Every afternoon now there is a stool kept for you under the locust tree. Today the old men are staking their tea cups on you.

ok.log: You win. The square goes silent. {npc} shakes your hand and demands a game every day for a year.

fail.log: You lose, well. The tea cups change hands. {npc} pours you one of the winnings.

choices.text: Play a game for fun, swapping sides halfway

effects.log: Neither of you knows who wins. The old men are scandalised. {npc} laughs till {he} coughs.

events.arc: The Chess Under the Locust Tree
events.text: {npc} cannot see the board well any more. {He} still comes to the tree and asks you to say the moves aloud.

effects.log: {npc} plays entirely by ear, and still wins. The square applauds the two of you.

choices.text: Carve a board with raised squares

effects.log: {npc} plays by touch. The first game on it, {npc} beats you in eleven moves, and is radiant.

events.text: {npc} sells kites from a stall by the bridge, every one a bird. {He} asks if you would test one: {his} legs are too old for running.

effects.log: It is a swallow. It flies like one. {npc} shouts instructions from the bridge, waving.

choices.text: Ask how the birds are made

effects.log: Split bamboo, glue from fish, paper from the next county. {npc} lets you try one wing.

events.text: {npc} has made a kite shaped like you, roughly, with your sword and your hat. It is the best seller on the stall.

effects.log: A small paper you flies over the bridge. The children cheer. {npc} sells forty that week.

choices.text: Ask for a share of the profit

effects.log: {npc} gives you one copper and a free kite. It is fair, somehow.

events.text: {npc}'s hands have grown stiff and {he} wants to pass the stall to someone who will keep the birds flying.

choices.text: Learn the craft in the evenings

effects.log: Your first bird is a sort of duck. Your tenth flies. {npc} says the stall is in good hands, eventually.
A quiet child from the bridge. {npc} grumbles for a week and then teaches the child everything.

events.text: {npc} sweeps the temple steps every morning, a hundred and eight of them, one leaf at a time. {He} offers you the second broom.

effects.log: A hundred and eight steps. By the top you are calmer than you have been in a year.

choices.text: Ask why one leaf at a time

effects.log: {npc} says if you sweep them all at once you miss the leaves. You think about it all day.

events.text: Autumn, and the temple steps are buried in leaves, and {npc} has hurt {his} wrist.

effects.log: It takes the whole day. {npc} sits at the top, telling you which leaves you missed.

choices.text: Bring the children of the lane to help

effects.log: Twenty children, twenty brooms, a leaf war. The steps are clean in an hour, and the leaves are everywhere else.

events.text: {npc} gives you the second broom to keep. {He} says it was waiting for someone to sweep with.

choices.text: Sweep the steps with {npc} on the first of every month

effects.log: You keep it up for years. {npc} says you sweep too fast still.

choices.text: Hang the broom in your house

effects.log: A broom on the wall is strange. You tell nobody why. {npc} knows.

events.text: {npc} sings at the washing stones by the river, and the whole bank goes quiet to listen. When {he} stops, everyone carries on. {He} has noticed you listening.

choices.text: Ask for the name of the song

effects.log: It has no name. It is the song for washing, {npc} says, and teaches you the first line.

ok.log: You get it nearly right. The bank laughs and claps. {npc} sings the next verse at you.

fail.log: Badly. The bank laughs. {npc} says nobody gets it right the first time.

events.text: {npc} has lost {his} voice to a cold, and the washing bank is silent and miserable, and {npc} asks if you will sing instead.

ok.log: You sing the washing song for a week. The bank keeps time with the paddles.

fail.log: You sing badly, and the bank sings with you out of pity, and it becomes a good morning anyway.

effects.log: {npc}'s voice is back in four days. The first thing {he} sings is rude, about you, and very fond.

events.text: A traveller from the capital hears {npc} at the washing stones and offers {him} a place singing in a great house. {npc} asks what you think.

effects.log: {npc} goes. A year later a letter: {he} sings the washing song in silk, and nobody understands it.
{npc} stays. The river would have missed {him}. So would you.

events.text: {npc}, who runs the ferry, keeps a ledger of every passenger, with a note: tall, smelled of fish, owed a copper. {He} wants to know what to write for you.

effects.log: Brave and handsome, you say. {npc} writes: says brave and handsome. Owes nothing.
Forty years of passengers. A famous general is listed as: seasick. You laugh for the whole crossing.

events.text: {npc} has found a passenger in the ledger, from thirty years ago, who owed a copper and never came back: the current county magistrate.

ok.log: The magistrate laughs, pays a copper and adds a silver for the story. {npc} writes it in the ledger: paid, late, generous.

fail.log: The magistrate is not amused. {npc} writes: still owes a copper. Also no sense of humour.

effects.log: You overpay. {npc} writes in the ledger: settled by a friend, change owed.

events.text: {npc} is giving up the ferry, and wants the ledger to go to someone who will keep it.

effects.log: Forty years of passengers on your shelf. You add a last entry, for {npc}: kind, owed everything.

choices.text: Give it to the county archive

mem.note: gave my ledger to the archive

effects.log: The archivist is thrilled. Scholars study it. One writes a book. {npc} says it has too many long words in it, and has it read aloud.

events.text: Every morning {npc} walks a songbird in a cage through the park, the cage swinging, the bird singing. {He} stops to ask if you have heard a bird sing like this one.

effects.log: {npc} tells you the bird's whole family history. It goes back further than most nobles.
The bird answers you. {npc} is amazed and somewhat jealous.

events.text: {npc}'s bird has escaped and is sitting in the very top of a pine in the park, singing, and will not come down.

ok.log: Near the top, the bird hops on your finger as if it had been waiting. {npc} weeps openly.

fail.log: You get halfway and slide. The bird flies down to {npc} by itself, to see what the noise was.

ok.log: It comes, to your whistle, not {npc}'s. {npc} forgives you, eventually.

fail.log: The bird ignores you, then comes down for a worm. {npc} pretends it was the whistle.

events.text: The old songbird is gone, of age, and {npc} still walks the empty cage through the park each morning out of habit, and asks if you would walk with {him}.

effects.log: You walk the park together, the empty cage swinging. {npc} whistles the bird's song. Other birds answer.
You paid 2 taels at the bird market. {npc} says it will never be as good, and walks it every morning, talking to it the whole way.

events.arc: The Tea Stall at the Crossroads
events.text: {npc} runs a tea stall at a crossroads with one bench and one kettle. {He} pours you a cup without asking, and charges nothing, because, {he} says, you looked like you needed it.

effects.log: The tea is bitter and good. {npc} talks about the weather in four directions.
You paid 1 tael and left it under the cup. {npc} finds it and shouts after you. You keep walking.

events.arc: The Tea Stall at the Crossroads
events.text: {npc}'s stall has been knocked over by a cart in the night, the kettle dented, the bench broken.

effects.log: A better bench than before. {npc} says it is too comfortable, people will never leave.
A big copper kettle. {npc} says the tea tastes different. Better, {he} admits, after a week.

events.arc: The Tea Stall at the Crossroads
events.text: You pass the crossroads after a long time away. {npc} has kept your cup, with your name scratched on it, on a nail behind the stall.

choices.text: Sit on your bench and drink from your cup

effects.log: The tea is the same. The bench is the same. {npc} talks about the weather in four directions.

choices.text: Ask whose other cups are on the nails

effects.log: Thirty cups, thirty regulars. {npc} tells you about every one. Seven of them are dead and {npc} still washes their cups.

events.text: {npc} has been building a boat in a barn for nine years, and has just realised it is too big to get out through the door.

effects.log: It still does not fit. You take off the wall. {npc} is delighted and horrified.
{npc} laughs until {he} has to sit in the boat. You both sit in the boat in the barn.

events.text: The barn wall is down, the boat is out, and {npc} wants you aboard for the first launch.

ok.log: It floats. It floats well. {npc} sails it straight into the reeds and is perfectly happy.

fail.log: It floats for a moment, then sits on the river bottom in shallow water. You both stand in it, waist deep, laughing.

choices.text: Watch from the bank and cheer

effects.log: It floats. The bank cheers. {npc} waves, loses an oar, and keeps waving.

events.text: {npc}'s boat is famous on the river now. {npc} has carved your name on the bow, beside the boat's, because, {he} says, you took the wall down.

choices.text: Go out on the river together

effects.log: A slow afternoon on the water. The barn, with its missing wall, is still standing. {npc} has never fixed it.

choices.text: Help {npc} build the second boat, measuring the door first

effects.log: You measure the door. {npc} measures the door. The second boat fits. {npc} is almost disappointed.

events.arc: The Poems on the Tavern Wall
events.text: The tavern wall is covered in poems by travellers. {npc}, at the next table, has been reading them aloud, terribly, and wants to know which is yours.

effects.log: {npc} reads yours aloud, terribly. The tavern applauds. You are not sure it was the poem.

ok.log: A poem about the bad wine and the good company. {npc} reads it twice and buys you a bowl of noodles.

fail.log: It does not scan. {npc} reads it aloud anyway, and makes it worse, and better.

events.arc: The Poems on the Tavern Wall
events.text: {npc} has started a poetry contest on the tavern wall, and has entered under a false name. {He} asks you to guess which one is {his}.

ok.log: The one about the goat. {npc} is crushed and delighted at once.

fail.log: You pick the one about the moon. It was the goat. {npc} is crushed you did not recognise {his} genius.

choices.text: Vote for {npc}'s anyway, whichever it is

effects.log: You win {npc} the contest by one vote, with a poem about a goat.

events.arc: The Poems on the Tavern Wall
events.text: The tavern is to be painted. {npc} wants to copy every poem on the wall before they are lost, and needs a second brush.

effects.log: Two hundred poems by dawn. Your poem and {npc}'s goat are side by side on the last page.

choices.text: Ask the owner to leave one wall unpainted

effects.log: The owner laughs and agrees. The poem wall stays. {npc} writes a new poem on it, about you.

events.text: {npc}, a blind masseur at the bathhouse, finds a knot in your shoulder that you have had for ten years, and asks what you have been carrying.

effects.log: You talk. {npc} works the knot out as you talk. You walk out lighter in more than one way.
{npc} laughs and says a sword sits lower than that. The knot goes anyway.

events.text: {npc}'s rent has been doubled by the bathhouse owner, and {npc} cannot pay it, and is going to have to leave.

ok.log: The owner backs down when half the customers threaten to bathe elsewhere. {npc} stays.

fail.log: The owner will not move. {npc} leaves, but half the customers follow {him} to a new room.

choices.text: Find {npc} a room of {his} own (3 taels)

effects.log: A small room on the canal. {npc}'s customers find it within a week.

events.text: {npc} has trained an apprentice, also blind, and wants you to be the apprentice's first customer, because, {npc} says, you have the worst shoulders in the province.

effects.log: The apprentice is very good, and very firm. {npc} gives instructions from a stool, delighted.

choices.text: Bring two friends with bad shoulders too

effects.log: Three bad shoulders. The apprentice is booked for a month. {npc} gives you a free session forever.

events.arc: Eleven Cats at the End of the Lane
events.text: {npc} lives at the end of the lane with eleven cats, and has decided one of them, a large orange one, has chosen you.

effects.log: The cat moves in and takes your bed. You sleep at the foot of it. {npc} visits to check on its happiness.

choices.text: Visit the cat at {npc}'s house instead

effects.log: You visit weekly. You learn the names of all eleven cats, and of {npc}'s three late spouses, all of whom liked cats.

events.arc: Eleven Cats at the End of the Lane
events.text: {npc} is ill in bed, and the eleven cats are hungry and loud, and {npc} asks if you will feed them.

choices.text: Feed the cats for a week

effects.log: Eleven cats, eleven opinions about fish. By the end of the week they follow you down the lane.

choices.text: Bring {npc} soup and feed the cats

effects.log: {npc} is up in a week. The cats are offended that the soup was not for them.

events.arc: Eleven Cats at the End of the Lane
events.text: {npc} says the cats have voted, and when {npc} is gone they are all to go to you.

effects.log: {npc} is very relieved. You are very worried. The cats are very calm.

choices.text: Suggest finding them homes now, together

effects.log: Eleven cats, eleven homes. {npc} interviews every family. Two families fail.

events.arc: The Old Soldier on the Wall
events.text: {npc}, an old soldier, sits on the town wall every evening and watches the north road. {He} has done it for thirty years. {He} says nobody ever asks why.

effects.log: A friend went up the north road in a war and never came back. {npc} is still waiting. You sit with {him} till dark.
{npc} drinks it without a word. The next evening there is a second stool on the wall.

events.arc: The Old Soldier on the Wall
events.text: {npc} has heard a rumour: an old soldier is living in a village up the north road who might be the friend.

ok.log: It is the friend, grey and lame. {npc} walks the whole north road to meet {him}. Neither of them can speak.

fail.log: It is not the friend. It is someone else's. You bring back that one's story, and {npc} sits with it.

choices.text: Take {npc} up the north road yourself

mem.note: took me up the north road

effects.log: A week's walk. {npc} looks at every face. You both come back, and {npc} sleeps well for the first time in years.

events.arc: The Old Soldier on the Wall
events.text: {npc} has stopped watching the north road, and has given you {his} stool on the wall.

choices.text: Sit on the stool, some evenings

effects.log: You watch the north road. Nobody comes. It is peaceful. {npc} would be pleased.

choices.text: Bring it down and keep it

effects.log: It sits in your house. Visitors ask about it. You tell them about the north road.

events.text: {npc}, a storyteller in the market, has been telling the same story for a month and has never finished it. The crowd is desperate. {He} catches your eye and asks what you think should happen.

ok.log: The next day, {npc} tells your ending to the crowd. The crowd roars. You say nothing, smugly.

fail.log: {npc} considers your ending, makes a face, and tells a better one. You recognise half of it.

choices.text: Say the story should never end

effects.log: {npc} laughs and says you understand the business.

events.text: {npc}'s voice has given out, and the crowd is restless, and {npc} pushes the fan and the wooden block into your hands.

ok.log: You tell it badly, then well. The crowd forgives you. {npc} whispers the names you forget.

fail.log: You lose the plot halfway. The crowd shouts suggestions. It becomes a better story.

choices.text: Tell a story of your own instead

effects.log: The crowd likes it. {npc} likes it so much {he} steals it the next week.

events.text: {npc} is retiring, and has decided at last to finish the story, with you in the front row.

effects.log: The ending is not the one anyone expected. It is better. The crowd sits in silence, then claps for an hour.

choices.text: Shout out the ending you gave {npc} years ago

effects.log: {npc} laughs and tells it your way. The crowd never knows which ending was meant.

events.text: {npc} grabs your sleeve in the crowd at the fair: {his} child is lost, a small one in a red jacket, and the crowd is enormous.

ok.log: A red jacket at the sugar figure stall. You are there in a moment. The child is eating a sugar dragon.

fail.log: You search for an hour. The child is found by a juggler, eating a sugar dragon.

choices.text: Go to the fair's drum and have it beaten

effects.log: The whole fair stops and looks down. A red jacket is pointed out in a minute.

events.text: {npc} and the child, who is bigger now and still wears red, come to thank you with a sugar dragon. The child insists you eat it first.

effects.log: The child gasps. {npc} laughs. You give the rest to the child, who eats it in two bites.

choices.text: Teach the child to stay put in crowds

effects.log: You teach the child a trick: stand by the biggest tree. The child listens, solemnly.

events.text: The child in red is grown, and works at the fair now, at the lost children's post, and {npc} wants you to see it.

mem.note: came to see my child's post

effects.log: A board of little red jackets for the lost to stand by. The grown child says it was your idea, really.

choices.text: Bring a crate of sugar dragons for the lost (2 taels)

effects.log: You paid 2 taels. Every lost child that year is found holding a dragon. {npc} says it is the best idea since the drum.

events.text: {npc}'s cart has gone into the ditch with a load of pots, and {npc} is sitting on the bank holding the one pot that survived.

effects.log: You and the mule. The mule does the most. {npc} gives you the surviving pot.
Forty pots, thirty-nine broken. You sort the pieces. {npc} says they can be sold as mosaic.

events.text: {npc} has opened a stall in town selling mosaic from broken pots, and it sells better than the pots ever did.

effects.log: A small mosaic of a mule. {npc} says it is the mule in the ditch. It looks determined.
A basket of your broken dishes. {npc} makes a mosaic of your kitchen. It is uncanny.

events.text: {npc} has been asked to make a mosaic for the temple floor, from the town's broken pots, and asks you to collect them.

effects.log: Every house gives something broken. The temple floor has a piece of every kitchen in town.

choices.text: Find the spot in the ditch and dig up the old pieces

effects.log: You find thirty pieces. {npc} puts them in the centre of the floor.

events.text: {npc} is getting married tomorrow, and the wedding cook has run off with the money for the pork, and {npc} is sitting on a rice sack in despair.

ok.log: Forty dishes, some very strange. The guests say it is the most interesting wedding they have been to.

fail.log: Forty dishes, some burnt. The guests eat everything. Weddings are like that.

choices.text: Find a cook in the next village

effects.log: The next village's cook comes, with the next village's pork. {npc} weeps into the rice sack.

events.text: {npc}'s first child has been born, and {npc} wants you to be the one who gives it its milk name.

effects.log: {npc} laughs until {he} cries and uses it, against all advice.

choices.text: Name the child after the next village

mem.note: named my child after the village

effects.log: The next village is honoured. It sends a pig.

events.text: The cook who ran away has come back, ten years later, to apologise to {npc}, and {npc} wants you there.

effects.log: The cook pays back the pork money, with interest, and cooks a feast. It is very good.

choices.text: Have the cook make the wedding feast again, properly

mem.note: had the wedding feast made again
