effects.log: You tell it your way. {npc} tells it {his} way. The young ones decide you were both terrible.

events.text: The town's tea contest. Your rival {npc} has entered a tea from the high mountains and is very confident.

choices.text: Enter a tea of your own

ok.log: Your tea wins. {npc} drinks a cup of it and says it is too sweet, and has another.

fail.log: {npc}'s tea wins. You drink a cup. It is very good.

effects.log: You judge fairly. {npc} comes second. {npc} accepts it, for once.

events.text: {npc}'s tea garden has been hit by frost, and the whole crop is lost.

effects.log: Your seedlings grow in {npc}'s garden. The next year's tea is a mix of both. It wins.
{npc} replants alone. {npc}'s next tea is very good. You hear it was made out of spite.

events.text: You and {npc} are the two oldest tea growers in the town, and the young ones want to know whose tea is the best.

effects.log: The young ones cannot decide. Neither can you. Neither can {npc}.
The blend wins the next contest. Nobody can tell who made it.

events.text: At the Mid-Autumn market, {npc} buys the last box of lotus mooncakes, just before you reach the stall, and then turns round and offers you half.

effects.log: You eat them on the bridge, looking at the moon. Neither of you mentions how long you sit.
{npc} insists harder. You end up eating them together anyway, on a bench.

events.text: Mid-Autumn again, and {npc} has made mooncakes, by hand, badly, with your name pressed into the top of one.

effects.log: It is too sweet and slightly burnt. You eat every crumb.

ok.log: Yours are better. {npc} is offended and very pleased.

fail.log: Yours are worse. {npc} says they are the best {he} has ever had, and lies well.

events.text: Mid-Autumn. {npc} has brought a mooncake to the bridge and broken it in two, and inside there is a slip of paper.

effects.log: It asks a question. You answer it on the bridge, under the moon.

choices.text: Eat the cake and say yes before reading

effects.log: {npc} laughs so much the slip falls in the river. It does not matter.

events.text: {npc}, who keeps the dry goods shop, has started writing little notes on your shopping lists: more ginger, you look tired.

effects.log: You write: thank you. You look tired too. {npc} adds a free packet of tea.
You buy more ginger. {npc} looks pleased about the ginger far beyond its importance.

events.text: The notes on the shopping lists have become letters. {npc} has started folding them into the packets of rice.

choices.text: Reply in a packet of salt

mem.note: found your letter in the salt

effects.log: {npc} finds it, laughs out loud in the shop, and reads it twice.

choices.text: Go to the shop and reply in person

effects.log: You stand in the shop for an hour. Three customers wait. None of them minds.

events.text: Today's list has one item on it, in {npc}'s hand: you.

effects.log: {npc} closes the shop for the afternoon, for the first time in eleven years.
You write: yes. {npc} pins it over the counter.

events.text: {npc}, next door, grows vegetables that climb over the wall into your yard. {He} asks if you mind. The beans are very good.

effects.log: The beans keep coming. So does {npc}, to pick them.
Your melons go over the wall. {npc} is delighted. The wall is now a garden.

events.text: A storm has knocked down the wall between your yard and {npc}'s.

effects.log: You rebuild it, lower, so you can talk over it.
One yard now, beans and melons. The neighbours have opinions.

events.text: {npc} has planted a row of flowers along where the wall used to be, in the shape of a path between your doors.

effects.log: You walk it to {npc}'s door. {npc} is waiting on the step.

choices.text: Plant flowers on your side to meet it

effects.log: The two rows meet in the middle. The neighbours stop having opinions and start having a wedding fund.

events.text: A wanderer with a sword, {npc}, is at the inn with a cut arm and no money, and the innkeeper is threatening to throw {him} out.

effects.log: {npc} bows, very stiffly, and says the debt will be paid. It is a promise.

ok.log: A good bandage. {npc} watches you work with an odd expression.

fail.log: A bad bandage. {npc} redoes it, laughing, and lets you watch.

events.text: {npc} has come back to the inn to repay the room, and keeps not leaving.

effects.log: {npc} says the noodles are good here. The noodles are not good here.

ok.log: {npc} is very good. You are better than you were.

fail.log: {npc} beats you easily, and helps you up, and stays another week.

events.text: {npc} is leaving the inn, for real, and stops at the door and asks if you have ever wanted to see the road.

effects.log: The road is long. {npc} talks the whole way. You do not mind at all.
{npc} looks at the road, and at you, and puts the sword down by the inn door.

events.text: {npc} has spent the winter's savings on a fur hat for you, because, {npc} says, your ears were always red. You notice {npc}'s own hat is full of holes.

mem.note: wore my hat and mended mine

effects.log: Two warm hats in one house. {npc} pretends the mending is not needed.
{npc} protests and loses. Your ears are red all winter. {npc}'s are not.

events.text: The fur hat has a hole now, and {npc} has noticed, and is pretending not to have.

mem.note: asked me to mend your hat

effects.log: {npc} mends it in an hour and spends three days complaining about how you treat hats.
{npc} wears it every day, even in spring, until a neighbour mentions it.

events.text: A cold winter. You find {npc} at the market with both old hats, the holes mended, trying to sell them to buy you a new one.

effects.log: You paid 1 tael. All three of you, {npc}, you and the hats, go home together.
{npc} looks at your ears. Your ears are red. {npc} buys you a scarf.

events.text: {npc} gives you an old ink stone, worn hollow in the middle by sixty years of grinding. {He} says every exam the family ever sat began on it.

effects.log: The ink is smoother than any you have used. Your characters look braver.
Two, {npc} says. And one who failed six times and became the happiest teacher in the county. That was {npc}.

events.text: {npc} watches you study on the old stone, every night, and brings you tea, every night, without a word.

effects.log: {npc} listens to the end and says the third paragraph is the one. It is.
{npc} is very surprised and drinks it slowly.

events.text: {npc} asks for the ink stone back, for one evening, to write a letter.

effects.log: {npc} writes a long letter to someone you never knew. You do not ask. {npc} tells you anyway.
In the morning the stone is back on your desk with a little poem on a slip beside it, about you.

events.text: When you were both small, you gave {npc} your ferry fare and walked the long way home. {npc} has never forgotten. Today {npc} has bought you a whole year of ferry tokens.

effects.log: You ride it all year. The ferryman knows your name. {npc} asks after the ferryman.

choices.text: Give half the tokens to children who cannot pay

effects.log: Twenty children ride free. {npc} says that was exactly the right thing, and is annoyed {he} did not think of it.

events.text: The ferry has sunk in a flood. The ferryman is safe. The tokens are useless. {npc} is laughing about it.

choices.text: Help raise money for a new ferry

effects.log: The whole bank gives a little. The new ferry has a plaque with the names. Yours is beside {npc}'s.

choices.text: Row people across in a borrowed boat

effects.log: You and {npc} row the bank across for a month. It is like being children again.

events.text: The new ferry's first passenger is {npc}'s grandchild, and {npc} gives you a token to give the child.

effects.log: The child crosses the river for the first time, holding your token. {npc} waves from the bank.
The child holds your hand the whole way and asks about the old ferry. You tell it.

events.arc: The Swarm in the Plum Tree
events.text: {npc}'s bees have swarmed into the top of the plum tree, a great humming beard, and {npc} wants them back in the hive.

ok.log: You shake the branch. The swarm falls in the basket. You are stung once, politely.

fail.log: The swarm moves to your head for a moment. Then it goes into the hive by itself.

choices.text: Wait with {npc} for them to settle

effects.log: {npc} tells you about bees for an hour. The bees go back to the hive in their own time.

events.arc: The Swarm in the Plum Tree
events.text: {npc}'s bees have made more honey than ever, and {npc} wants you to sell it in the market.

ok.log: Every jar sold. {npc} splits the money exactly in half.

fail.log: Half the jars sold. The other half you eat, with {npc}, over a winter.

choices.text: Give it away to the neighbours

effects.log: The whole lane is sticky and grateful. {npc} says the bees approve.

events.arc: The Swarm in the Plum Tree
events.text: {npc} asks if you will take one hive, to keep the bees in the family.

effects.log: The bees come to your yard. They seem to know you. {npc} visits them every week.
A whole season of lessons. Then the hive, and a veil, and a lot of advice.

events.text: {npc} has had a baby, and the baby will not sleep, and {npc} has not slept for a month, and asks if you would hold it for one night.

effects.log: You walk the room until dawn. The baby sleeps on your shoulder at the very end. {npc} sleeps eleven hours.

choices.text: Sing it the old song from your childhood

ok.log: The baby sleeps at the second verse. {npc} sleeps at the third.

mem.note: tried to sing my baby down

fail.log: The baby joins in, loudly. It is a long night, but a funny one.

events.text: {npc}'s baby is walking now, and has decided you are its favourite, and cries when you leave.

effects.log: The child eats on your lap and gives you half of everything, chewed.
Hide and seek. The child hides in the same place every time. You never find it.

events.text: {npc}'s child is old enough for school, and {npc} wants you to walk the child there on the first day.

effects.log: The child holds your hand all the way, and lets go at the door without looking back. {npc} cries for both of you.

choices.text: Buy the child a brush (1 tael)

effects.log: The child writes their first character with it, and brings it to show you.

events.text: The river is rising, and {npc}'s house is on the low bank, and {npc} will not leave without {his} furniture, and asks for your back.

effects.log: Two days of chairs and chests. Everything is saved, including a very ugly vase.

choices.text: Carry {npc} uphill and come back for the furniture

effects.log: {npc} is furious and safe. You go back. You save the ugly vase.

events.text: The flood is down. {npc}'s house is full of mud. {npc} is standing in the doorway with a shovel.

effects.log: A week of mud. The house comes back. {npc} is smiling by the end.

choices.text: Help {npc} build on the high bank

effects.log: A new house, on stilts, on the high bank. {npc} grumbles and moves in.

events.text: Another flood, a big one, and {npc}'s house on the high bank is dry, and full of the low bank's families.

effects.log: Twenty people in one house. Your rice feeds them all for a week.

ok.log: A long day in the water. Everybody reaches the high bank.

fail.log: You are knocked down twice. Everybody reaches the high bank anyway.

events.text: {npc}, the post rider, has a letter for a village that no longer exists, and does not know what to do with it. {He} asks if you can read the name.

choices.text: Read the name and find the family

ok.log: The family moved to the next valley. The letter is from a son who left forty years ago. They weep.

fail.log: You cannot find them. {npc} keeps the letter, in case.

choices.text: Read the letter, carefully, to see who it is for

effects.log: It is for a mother, from a child at the frontier. You and {npc} decide to keep looking.

events.text: {npc} has found the family at last, and wants you there when the letter is handed over.

effects.log: An old woman takes the letter and holds it a long time before opening it.

choices.text: Read it aloud for the old woman

effects.log: The old woman cannot read. You read it aloud. It is a love letter from a soldier, and the old woman was the one it was for.

events.text: {npc} is retiring, and has a box of letters that were never delivered, and asks you to help find them homes.

effects.log: A year of searching. Forty letters delivered. Some of them are forty years late.

choices.text: Write to the county for help

effects.log: The county sends a clerk. {npc} trains the clerk. The letters are delivered.

events.text: {npc}, the tailor, has twenty robes to finish for a wedding by tomorrow, and needles enough for two, and hands enough for one.

ok.log: Your stitches are uneven. The wedding guests do not notice.

fail.log: Your stitches are terrible. {npc} unpicks them at dawn, laughing, and finishes in time.

effects.log: Ten needles, ten neighbours, one night. Twenty robes by dawn.

events.text: {npc} has made you a robe, for nothing, the best one {he} ever made.

choices.text: Wear it to the next festival

effects.log: Everyone asks who made it. You send them to {npc}, who is booked for a year.

choices.text: Save it for a special day

effects.log: It hangs on your wall. {npc} says that is the highest compliment and the worst use of a robe.

events.text: {npc}'s eyes are going, and {he} cannot thread a needle, and asks you to thread a hundred for {him}, to last the month.

effects.log: A hundred needles in a pin cushion. {npc} finishes the month's work and asks for another hundred.
The apprentice threads the needles. {npc} teaches the stitches. A good arrangement.

events.text: {npc} turns up with a scraped knee from falling off the same wall you fell off at the same age, and wants to compare scars.

effects.log: Yours is bigger. {npc} says {his} is deeper. The argument lasts all afternoon and is very happy.
Water, a clean rag and a lecture. {npc} says you sound exactly like the old people, and lets you do it anyway.

events.text: {npc} has climbed the wall again, on purpose this time, to show you it can be done without falling.

mem.note: sat on the wall with me

ok.log: You both sit on top, legs dangling, kings of the lane.

fail.log: You fall off. {npc} laughs so hard {he} nearly falls too. Now you have two scars.

effects.log: {npc} does not fall, and pretends not to have noticed you standing there, arms out.

events.text: The wall is being pulled down to widen the lane, and {npc} has come to take one stone from it.

effects.log: Two stones from the wall that gave you both your scars. {npc} puts {his} on the family shrine, which is not what it is for.

choices.text: Sit on the wall one last time

mem.note: sat on the wall one last time

effects.log: The workers wait, amused, while two grown people sit on a wall comparing knees.

events.text: {npc} has drawn a map of the hills with a red cross on it, and swears there is treasure, and wants you to come and dig.

effects.log: A whole day of digging. You find a broken pot, a coin and a very surprised badger. {npc} declares it treasure.
Your map is accurate. {npc}'s is more exciting. You use {npc}'s.

events.text: {npc} has found the coin from the dig is very old, and a pawnbroker has offered good silver for it.

choices.text: Sell it and split the silver

effects.log: A small fortune, for children. {npc} spends {his} share on sweets for the whole lane.

choices.text: Keep it as the family treasure

effects.log: The coin goes on the shrine. Every guest is told the story of the badger.

events.text: {npc} has found the old map in a chest and wants to go back to the red cross, grown up, with a proper spade.

effects.log: You dig where you dug before. A second coin. You both sit in the hole and laugh like children.

choices.text: Bury something for the next children

effects.log: A jar with two coins and a note. You mark it on the old map and leave the map in the chest.

events.text: {npc} has borrowed your best robe for an important day, without asking, and comes back in it with a tea stain on the sleeve and a very good story.

effects.log: The story is worth the stain. Possibly two stains. You laugh until {npc} gets hiccups.
{npc} washes it badly and returns it with a sweet in the pocket, as an apology.

events.text: {npc} needs the robe again, for an even more important day, and this time asks first, very politely.

choices.text: Lend it, and lend a hat

mem.note: lent me the robe and hat

effects.log: {npc} looks magnificent. The important day goes well. The hat is never seen again.

choices.text: Go with {npc} to the important day

effects.log: It is a meeting with a stern merchant. You sit at the back and pull faces. {npc} gets the job anyway.

events.text: {npc} has had a robe made for you, the exact same cut, with no stain, and wants to swap back for the old one.

effects.log: {npc} keeps the old stained robe and wears it to every important day for luck.

choices.text: Keep both, and lend the new one

effects.log: {npc} borrows the new one within the month. It comes back with a story.

events.text: Caught in a downpour on the way home, {npc} holds a coat over both your heads. It covers neither of you well.

mem.note: ran home in the rain with me

effects.log: You arrive soaked through, both of you, and are made to stand by the stove like wet dogs.
An hour under the eaves, talking about nothing. The rain stops. You walk home slower than you need to.

events.text: Rain again, years later, and {npc} turns up at your door with the same old coat, and nothing else.

mem.note: let me in out of the rain

effects.log: Tea, a dry robe, and a long evening. {npc} says the coat still covers nobody.

choices.text: Walk {npc} home under a proper umbrella

effects.log: You walk {npc} home dry. At the door {npc} gives you the coat, for next time.

events.text: You find the old coat in a chest. You take it round to {npc}'s house, and it is raining.

choices.text: Hold it over both your heads again

mem.note: held the coat over us again

effects.log: It still covers neither of you. You walk round the block anyway, for no reason.

mem.note: gave the coat to my children

effects.log: The children take turns under it in the yard, getting wet, delighted.

events.text: The grown-ups are out, and {npc} has decided the two of you will cook dinner, and the rice is already smoking.

ok.log: You scrape off the black. The middle is fine. The grown-ups are amazed.

fail.log: It is all black. You eat pickles. You both swear never to tell, and tell everyone within a week.

effects.log: The second pot is perfect. The first pot is buried in the garden, a secret between you.

events.text: {npc} has learned to cook properly from a neighbour and invites you to a dinner, with no burning at all.

choices.text: Eat every dish and praise them

effects.log: Seven dishes. {npc} watches every bite. At the end {npc} serves, as a joke, one black lump of rice.
You cook the rice. It is perfect. {npc} pretends to be disappointed.

events.text: {npc}'s household is large now, and the New Year dinner is at {npc}'s, and {npc} wants you in the kitchen, for old times.

mem.note: cooked the New Year with me

effects.log: Twelve dishes, two cooks, one small kitchen. Nothing burns. You both nearly miss it.

choices.text: Burn one pot of rice on purpose

mem.note: burnt the rice for old times

effects.log: The black rice is served in the middle of the table. Only the two of you know why it is there.

events.text: {npc} has caught a cricket and named it General, and keeps it in a little bamboo cage, and wants to know if you have caught one too.

choices.text: Catch one and name it Emperor

effects.log: General and Emperor sing at each other all night. The whole house is awake. Nobody minds.
Cucumber, grass, a drop of water. General sings louder. {npc} credits you.

events.text: General has stopped singing, and {npc} is worried, and has wrapped the cage in a scarf.

choices.text: Put the cage in the sun

effects.log: In the warmth, General sings again, a little hoarse. {npc} hugs you, which never happens.

choices.text: Let General go in the long grass

effects.log: You open the cage together. General walks out slowly and sings once from the grass. {npc} is brave about it.

events.text: Autumn, and {npc} brings you a new bamboo cage, very fine, and says there is no cricket in it yet, because you have to catch it together.

choices.text: Go out into the long grass

effects.log: Two grown people on hands and knees in a field. You catch one and name it General the Second.

choices.text: Hang the empty cage by the window

effects.log: Crickets sing outside the window all autumn. The cage stays empty. {npc} says that is a good way too.

events.text: {npc} gives you a letter, sealed, and says it was written years ago, after a quarrel, and never sent. {npc} would like you to read it now.

effects.log: It is a furious letter about a broken kite. You both laugh so hard the neighbours look in.
It is a sad letter, and a kind one, about how much {npc} missed you that year. You go round that evening.

events.text: You write {npc} a letter you should have sent long ago, and walk it round in person.

effects.log: {npc} reads it at the door and does not say anything, and then makes tea for an hour.

choices.text: Push it under the door and walk away

effects.log: The next morning there is a reply under your own door.

events.text: {npc} has kept both letters in a box with a lock, and gives you one of the two keys.

choices.text: Keep the key on your belt

effects.log: Neither of you ever opens the box again. Both of you keep your keys.

choices.text: Add a third letter to the box

effects.log: You write about today. {npc} reads it, nods, and locks the box.

events.text: {npc} dares you to swim across the river at the wide place, where the old people say nobody should.

ok.log: You both make it, gasping, and lie on the far bank in the sun like seals.

fail.log: The current is strong. You both turn back halfway and agree never to tell.

choices.text: Say no, and walk round by the bridge

effects.log: {npc} swims. You walk. You arrive first. {npc} never forgives the bridge.

events.text: A child from the lane is caught in the current at the wide place, and {npc} is already running.

ok.log: You get the child between you and kick for the bank. The lane carries you all home.

fail.log: The current spins you, but you reach the bank, the child held up between you.

choices.text: Throw them the rope from the jetty

effects.log: The rope reaches. {npc} grabs it with one hand and the child with the other.

events.text: {npc} has built a little jetty at the wide place, with a rope and a bell, and wants you to hang the bell.

effects.log: Nobody drowns at the wide place again. Children ring the bell for no reason. Nobody minds.

choices.text: Teach the lane's children to swim there

effects.log: A summer of lessons. {npc} shouts from the jetty. Every child learns.

events.arc: The Lantern That Would Not Light
events.text: The Lantern Festival, and {npc}'s lantern will not light: the wick is wet, and everyone else is already walking to the river.

effects.log: You tip your lantern to {npc}'s. It catches. You walk to the river with two lights.

choices.text: Run home for a dry wick

effects.log: You run both ways. You arrive at the river last, out of breath, and {npc} has waited for you.

events.arc: The Lantern That Would Not Light
events.text: The festival again, and this year {npc} has made two lanterns, one for each of you, and kept the wicks in a box all year.

effects.log: It is shaped like a rabbit and is very lopsided. You carry it like a banner.
Halfway to the river you swap. Neither of you could say why. It feels right.

events.arc: The Lantern That Would Not Light
events.text: Grown, both of you, and the Lantern Festival, and {npc} hands you a dry wick before you even ask.

choices.text: Light them from each other's flame

effects.log: Two flames, one from the other. You walk to the river, slowly, the long way.

choices.text: Float them together on the river

effects.log: Two lights going down the river side by side. You watch until you cannot tell which is which.

events.text: {npc} is in bed with a long fever and is bored beyond words, and asks if you will come and sit with {him}.

effects.log: Every story you know, some of them twice. {npc} falls asleep in the middle of the best one.

choices.text: Play a game of stones on the blanket

effects.log: The stones roll off every time {npc} coughs. You play anyway, and {npc} wins.

events.text: Now you are the one with the fever, and {npc} turns up at your bedside with a basket.

choices.text: See what is in the basket

effects.log: Soup, oranges, and the game of stones. {npc} lets you win, badly.
{npc} tells you your own best story back, wrongly. You correct it, and are better by evening.

events.text: {npc} has a cold, a small one, and has sent word that it is very serious and requires a visit.

effects.log: The cold is very small. {npc} is very pleased. You stay for dinner.

choices.text: Go with the game of stones

effects.log: You play all evening. {npc} wins, and is cured, apparently by winning.

events.text: Behind a frozen waterfall you find a pool of steaming water, warm as a bath, with three monkeys already in it. They look at you as if you are late.

effects.log: The monkeys move over, grudgingly. You soak for an hour. Your old aches melt away.
You sit on a warm rock and watch them. One of them throws a pine cone at you, kindly.

events.text: Back at the hot spring in a hard winter. A woodcutter has slipped on the ice beside it and cannot walk.

ok.log: A long walk on ice. The woodcutter's family feeds you for three days.

fail.log: You both slip twice. You get there in the end, cold and bruised.

choices.text: Bathe the leg in the spring first

effects.log: The warm water helps. The woodcutter limps home on your arm.

events.text: The hot spring again. Somebody has built a little roof over it and a bench, and carved a notice: for the monkeys first.

effects.log: You wait an hour. The monkeys finish, and one of them leaves you a pine cone on the bench.

choices.text: Add a line to the notice

effects.log: You carve: and then the woodcutters. Next time someone has carved: and then everyone.

events.text: A scroll case is wedged high in a lightning-split pine by the road. Somebody put it there on purpose.

ok.log: Inside, a scroll of breathing exercises in an old hand, and a note: for whoever climbs.

fail.log: You slide down the trunk. The case stays where it is. Somebody meant it to be hard.

choices.text: Leave it for whoever put it there

effects.log: You leave it. Somebody may be coming back for it.

events.text: The pine by the road again. A young traveller is trying to climb it, badly, and has fallen twice.

effects.log: You give a leg up. The traveller reaches the case, opens it, and starts to cry. It was a grandparent's.
The traveller climbs it alone, which matters to them. They wave the scroll from the top.

events.text: A scroll case in the split pine again, a new one. The note inside says: from one who climbed, for whoever climbs next.

choices.text: Read it and put it back

effects.log: A page of good advice in a young hand. You add a line and put it back.
You leave a scroll of what you know. The pine becomes known along the road as the Teaching Tree.

events.text: In a narrow valley, every tree has a small bronze bell hanging from it, and the wind plays them all at once.

effects.log: The note goes all the way down the valley. A bell far away answers.
It takes an hour. The bells ring anyway, for the wind, not for you.

events.text: The bell valley. A bell has fallen and lies cracked in the grass.

effects.log: It rings flat. The valley sounds better with one bell wrong.

choices.text: Take it to a bell-maker (2 taels)

effects.log: You paid 2 taels. The bell-maker says the valley is famous among bell-makers, and recasts it for half price.

events.text: The valley of bells, and a family is hanging a new bell on a young tree, for a child born that year.

effects.log: The child, a year old, grabs the bell and rings it. The whole valley answers.
Every child of the valley has a bell. When the child goes away, the bell keeps ringing for them. You think about it a long time.

events.text: The short way across the salt marsh is a line of posts in the mud. A fog is coming in from the sea.

ok.log: Post to post, just ahead of the fog. You reach the far side as it closes behind you.

fail.log: You lose a post in the fog and wade knee-deep for an hour. You find the way, eventually, smelling of the sea.

choices.text: Wait for the fog to pass

effects.log: The fog sits for a day. You eat dried fish with a heron for company.

events.text: The salt marsh again. Some of the posts have fallen, and the fog is coming.

effects.log: A cold, muddy day. The line is straight again. A fisher passing says you have saved lives.

choices.text: Mark the path with white stones

effects.log: White stones between the posts, visible in fog. The marsh people like it.

events.text: Fog on the salt marsh, and a voice calling out there, lost.

choices.text: Walk out along the posts and call back

ok.log: You meet a lost peddler halfway and bring them in by voice and post.

fail.log: It takes half the night, but the peddler is found, wet and grateful.

choices.text: Light a fire on the shore

effects.log: The peddler walks toward the fire and reaches it at dawn.

events.text: On a hill pass lies a stone guardian, toppled long ago, face down in the grass, its sword arm broken off.

effects.log: It takes all your strength. The stone face looks at the sky again. It seems relieved.
A rice cake by the stone hand. The wind on the pass goes quiet.

events.text: The pass with the guardian. A village mason is there, measuring the broken arm.

effects.log: The new arm is fitted. The guardian holds a sword over the pass again.
A general who held the pass five hundred years ago, the mason says, against an army, with forty people.

events.text: The pass, and the guardian standing tall on its plinth again, and at its feet, small offerings from travellers.

effects.log: A rice cake by the stone foot. You bow. It may be the light, but the face looks satisfied.

choices.text: Sit and rest in its shadow

effects.log: You rest an hour. The pass is quiet. You feel watched over.

events.text: At dawn on a lotus lake the flowers open all at once with a small sound, like breath. You have never heard anything like it.

effects.log: You stay till noon. You come back more patient than you went.

choices.text: Gather seeds from the old pods

effects.log: A pocketful of lotus seeds. They taste green and sweet.

events.text: The lotus lake has been drained by a landowner who wants a rice field. Only mud and old stems are left.

choices.text: Save some roots in a jar

effects.log: You dig out three roots and keep them in a water jar.

ok.log: The landowner relents, astonished at being argued with. The lake is let back in.

fail.log: The landowner will not listen. You save a few roots anyway.

events.text: You have kept lotus roots in a jar for years, and a village nearby has dug a new pond and needs a start.

effects.log: The pond flowers in two summers. At dawn it makes the same small sound.

choices.text: Plant them yourself with the village

effects.log: A muddy day of planting. The children of the village call it your pond.

events.text: Fresh snow, and the tracks of a big wolf along the same path you are walking, going the same way.

ok.log: The tracks lead to a den with three cubs. You back away quietly, very carefully.

fail.log: The wolf finds you first. You both back away, but not before you fall in a drift.

effects.log: An extra hour of snow. You hear a howl far behind you, and are glad.

events.text: A village at the edge of the forest is setting traps for the wolf that took a sheep.

effects.log: A higher fence, a bell on the gate. No more sheep are taken, and nothing is trapped.
The traps catch nothing all winter. The wolf is cleverer than the village.

events.text: Snow, the same path, and the tracks of a big wolf and three smaller ones, all going the same way as you.

effects.log: The wolves cross the path ahead of you, look at you, and go on. You feel oddly honoured.
You wait an hour. The tracks go into the forest. You walk on in the quiet.

events.text: On the river ferry there is a cat who rides back and forth all day and gets off at neither bank. The ferryman says it has done so for nine years.

choices.text: Feed the cat a bit of fish

effects.log: The cat accepts it with dignity and sits on your foot for the rest of the crossing.
The cat came on board as a kitten and simply never got off. The ferryman says it is the real owner.

events.text: The ferry again, and the old cat has a kitten with it, also riding back and forth.

effects.log: Two cats on your feet. The ferryman says you are now family.

choices.text: Take a kitten home, if it will come

ok.log: The kitten walks off the ferry with you, the first of its line to do so.

fail.log: The kitten refuses to leave the ferry. It knows its place.

events.text: The ferry again. The old cat is gone, and the kitten, grown, rides back and forth in its place.

choices.text: Feed it a bit of fish

effects.log: It sits on your foot, exactly as its mother did.

choices.text: Bring a cushion for the ferry

effects.log: A cushion for the ferry cat. The ferryman laughs and puts it in the bow.

events.text: At the top of a long mountain pass there is a wooden box on a post, full of letters left by travellers for other travellers to carry down.

effects.log: The letter is to a farm in the valley you are heading for. You deliver it. You are given lunch.

choices.text: Leave a letter of your own

effects.log: You leave a letter to nobody in particular. Someone will carry it somewhere.

events.text: A letter in the mountain box has your name on it. Somebody, somewhere, wrote back.

effects.log: It is from a traveller who found your letter and carried it to the sea. It describes the sea. You read it twice.

choices.text: Carry it down to read at home

effects.log: You read it by your own lamp, slowly. It is a kind letter from a stranger.

events.text: The postbox on the pass has rotted and fallen, and the letters are scattered in the grass.

choices.text: Gather them and build a new box

effects.log: A new box, and every letter in it, dried and sorted. Travellers will carry them on.
A month of walking to farms and towns. Some of the letters are years late. Every one is welcome.

events.arc: The Tea House in the Clouds
events.text: High on a mountain, above the clouds, there is a tea house with one table and one old keeper, who pours for you without asking.

choices.text: Drink slowly and look down at the clouds

effects.log: The clouds move under you like the sea. The tea is the best you have ever had.

choices.text: Ask how the keeper gets the tea up here

effects.log: On their back, the keeper says, once a month, for forty years. You feel lazy.

events.arc: The Tea House in the Clouds
events.text: Back at the cloud tea house. The keeper is too old now to carry the tea up, and the shelf is empty.

choices.text: Carry up a month of tea

effects.log: A hard climb with a heavy basket. The keeper pours you the first cup, without asking.

choices.text: Find a young carrier in the village below

effects.log: A strong, cheerful youth. The keeper grumbles, and teaches the youth the pouring.

events.arc: The Tea House in the Clouds
events.text: The tea house in the clouds, and a new keeper pours for you, the youth from the village, grown.

choices.text: Drink and ask after the old keeper

effects.log: The old keeper lives in the village below and comes up once a year, slowly, to complain about the tea.

choices.text: Leave a coin for the next traveller's cup (1 tael)

effects.log: You paid 1 tael. The next traveller up the mountain will drink for free.

events.text: The plank bridge over the gully groans under your first step. One plank is plainly rotten.

ok.log: You make it across. Behind you, the plank falls into the gully.

fail.log: Your foot goes through. You haul yourself out, scraped, and cross on hands and knees.

effects.log: Half a day round. You tell the village headman about the plank.

events.text: The bridge over the gully again. A cart is about to cross it.

effects.log: You stand in the road and wave your arms. The carter is furious until you show the planks.
You and the carter lay new planks from the cart's own load. The cart crosses.

events.text: A new stone bridge over the gully, and the carter from that day is on it, with a cart, waving.

effects.log: The carter shouts that the bridge should be named after you. Nobody else hears.
Every stone is sound. You stamp on one in the middle, for luck.

events.text: A snake is coiled on the sunny path ahead, not moving, right where you need to step.

effects.log: Half an hour. It leaves. You were in no hurry, it turns out.

ok.log: Over, and gone. It does not even wake.

fail.log: It bites your ankle. It is not poisonous. It is very painful.

events.text: A child on the same path is staring at a snake on the warm stones, frozen.

effects.log: You lift the child back by the shoulders. The snake goes on sleeping.

choices.text: Shoo the snake off with a stick

ok.log: The snake slides away into the grass. The child cheers.

fail.log: The snake strikes the stick, not you. You both jump back.

events.text: The children of the village call the sunny path the snake path now, and ask you to show them how to walk it.

choices.text: Teach them to watch the stones

effects.log: Look before you step. The children turn it into a game, and nobody is bitten that summer.

choices.text: Tell them the story of the frozen child

effects.log: The children love it. The grown child, who is now a carpenter, tells it better.

events.text: A squall comes over the lake while you are in a small boat, and the waves start coming over the side.

ok.log: You make the shore, soaked and shaking. The boat is half full.

fail.log: The boat swamps near the shore. You wade the rest, pulling it.

choices.text: Bail and let the wind take you

effects.log: You bail all afternoon and land on the wrong shore, alive.

events.text: A squall on the lake again, and a fisher's boat is overturned, with the fisher clinging to it.

ok.log: You reach the fisher and haul them in. The village fishers buy you dinner for a month.

fail.log: You nearly overturn too, but you get the fisher to shore.

choices.text: Throw a line from the jetty

effects.log: Three throws. The third reaches. The fisher is pulled in along the rope.

events.text: The fisher you pulled from the lake has made you a small boat, very steady, with a high side.

choices.text: Take it out on a calm day

effects.log: It is the steadiest boat on the lake. You fish all afternoon.

choices.text: Give it to the village for rescues

effects.log: It is painted red and kept by the jetty. It is used twice that year.

events.arc: The Carp in the Long Pond
events.text: {npc} is nobody's idea of an important person in this house, and has spent forty years looking after the carp in the long pond. You once pulled {him} out of that pond in front of the guests. Today {he} comes up the steps dripping, holding the old gold one in a bucket, and says it is yours.

mem.note: thanked me where people could hear

effects.log: The stewards look away, as they do. {npc} stands a good deal straighter than usual, still dripping.

choices.text: Carry the bucket back down together

mem.note: carried the bucket back with me

effects.log: The carp goes back. {npc} says it is still yours, and that it knows it now.

events.arc: The Carp in the Long Pond
events.text: The steward wants the long pond filled in for a new reception hall. There is a drawing. {npc} has seen the drawing, and is sitting on the edge of the pond with {his} shoes off, not saying anything to anyone.

choices.text: Have a word with the steward

mem.note: spoke to the steward for me

effects.log: The reception hall moves forty paces east. Nobody can say why, and the steward no longer meets {npc}'s eye.

choices.text: Take your shoes off and sit down too

mem.note: sat by the pond with me

effects.log: It is the first hour all season that nobody has asked you for anything. The drawing is not mentioned.

events.arc: The Carp in the Long Pond
events.text: {npc} cannot manage the steps to the water now. {He} has written out the names of all sixty carp, and which of them bite, and is looking for someone in this great house who will take the paper seriously.

mem.note: learned the names of my carp

effects.log: You feed them yourself for a month. Several of them bite. {npc} is very pleased about that.

choices.text: Find a young servant with patience, and pay for it

mem.note: found someone to keep my carp

effects.log: A kitchen child with an excellent memory. {npc} holds an examination every week and is merciless.

events.arc: The Keys of the Inner Court
events.text: {npc} has held the keys of the inner court since before anyone now living was born, and no decision here has ever been made without {him}. Today {he} takes one small key off the ring and presses it into your hand. It opens nothing you can find. {He} says that is a debt paid, and will not explain.

effects.log: You try every door you are allowed near, and several you are not. {npc} hears about each one by supper.

choices.text: Wear it, and do not ask

mem.note: wore my key and did not ask

effects.log: The old servants notice it at your belt before you reach the gate. They start telling you things.

events.arc: The Keys of the Inner Court
events.text: You find the lock at last: a small lacquer box in a wall of the old linen room. Inside is every note you ever wrote as a child to get out of lessons. {npc} is behind you with a lamp. {He} walks very quietly for someone that age.

mem.note: read the old notes aloud with me

effects.log: You have been a dreadful liar for a long time. {npc} laughs until a maid comes to see if anyone has died.
{npc} looks at you for some time. Then {he} tells you a little about the house, and you do not sleep well.

events.arc: The Keys of the Inner Court
events.text: {npc} has begun to forget which key is which, and has told nobody. {He} sits with the ring in {his} lap and asks you, as if it were nothing, to read the tags to {him}, because the light is so poor. It is noon.

choices.text: Read them, and say nothing of the light

mem.note: read me the tags and said nothing

effects.log: You read all forty. {He} repeats each one after you. Nobody else in the house ever learns of it.

choices.text: Offer to carry the ring on {his} rounds

effects.log: {npc} allows it, as a favour to you, and says so loudly to everyone you meet.

events.text: Every head and heir of the house hangs in the long hall, and every one looks as if they had swallowed a stone. {npc} has paid a painter, with {his} own silver, to do you, and has told the painter you are to be smiling. It is causing a certain amount of talk. {He} says it is what {he} owes you.

effects.log: It takes nine days and your face hurts. The elders walk past it very quickly.

mem.note: sat for the painter with me

effects.log: The painter has never done two in one frame. {npc} complains about the cost for a year, with great satisfaction.

events.text: An elder has had the smiling portrait moved to a corridor behind the kitchens, to protect the dignity of the hall. {npc} has found out, and has been eating {his} meals in that corridor for a week, on a stool, in full court dress.

mem.note: brought a stool to the corridor

effects.log: The kitchen staff are thrilled. By the end of the month half the junior cousins are eating there.

choices.text: Have it carried back to the hall

effects.log: You do it at noon, with everyone watching. The elder writes a letter, then thinks better of it.

events.text: {npc}'s own portrait wants painting, as they all must before the end, and {he} has sent the court painter away twice. {He} says the man keeps asking {him} to look dignified. {He} would rather you came and made {him} laugh, and got it over with.

choices.text: Tell the story of the corridor

mem.note: made me laugh for the painter

effects.log: It takes four tellings. The painter is very quick. It is the only face in the hall that looks as if it had ever been in a room with anyone.

choices.text: Sit with {him}, and let the man paint what is there

mem.note: sat with me while I was painted

effects.log: Neither of you talks much. The picture is not dignified, or undignified. You can hardly look at it, later.

events.arc: The Seating at the Long Table
events.text: Where people sit at the New Year table is settled by {npc}, who has done it for thirty years with a box of little wooden tags, and has started two feuds and ended four. You stood up for {him} once when it did not pay. This year your tag has moved three places up, for no reason {he} will admit to.

choices.text: Sit where you are put, and watch the room

effects.log: By the second course you have worked out who has noticed, and which of them mind. It is a very good education.
{npc} moves it up again before the soup. This happens twice more. Neither of you ever mentions it.

events.arc: The Seating at the Long Table
events.text: Two old branches of the house are not speaking, and each has told {npc} that it will not sit below the other. {npc} has the tags spread out on the floor, and has been sitting among them since breakfast. {He} wants a second opinion and does not want it known.

effects.log: {npc} looks at you as if you had suggested setting fire to the hall. Then {he} looks at the tags for a long time.

choices.text: Offer to sit between them yourself

effects.log: It is the longest dinner of your life. Nobody draws a weapon, and {npc} sends up something very nice for your stomach.

events.arc: The Seating at the Long Table
events.text: {npc} has decided who will have the box of tags after {him}. {He} has told nobody, and has begun, this year, to leave certain of them where you will find them, with small notes on the back about who cannot be trusted near the wine.

effects.log: Thirty years of who hates whom, in a very small hand. You will never enjoy a banquet again, and you will never be surprised at one.

choices.text: Say you are not the person for it

effects.log: {npc} nods, and leaves the next one in your shoe.

events.text: There are servants for it, but {npc} dusts the ancestral tablets of the house with {his} own hand on the first of the month, and has decided you are old enough to hold the cloth. There are three hundred and twelve. {He} tells you something rude about each.

effects.log: The founder's brother, it seems, was afraid of geese. This is not in the official history.

mem.note: asked which of them I liked

effects.log: {npc} stops, with the cloth in {his} hand, and tells you. It takes the whole morning, and you get no further along the row.

events.text: One tablet in the back row is turned to the wall, and always has been. Today {npc} dusts it anyway, turns it round for a moment, reads it, and turns it back. {He} knows you saw.

effects.log: {npc} tells you the name, and what was done, and who decided. {He} says the house was wrong about half of it, and that you are not to say so yet.

choices.text: Take the cloth and dust the next one

effects.log: You go on down the row. At the end {npc} gives you a look you have not seen before, and it seems you have passed something.

events.text: {npc}'s hands will not hold the steps now. {He} sits below with a list and calls out each name as you dust, and the rude part, in case you have forgotten. The young cousins have started coming to listen, and the elders have started to object.

mem.note: let the children come and listen

effects.log: Next month there are eleven children and a very nervous steward. The founder's brother and the geese have become well known.

choices.text: Keep it between the two of you

effects.log: The hall is very quiet. {npc} gets through all three hundred and twelve, and the last one is the kindest.

events.text: Nobody outside would believe it, but this house runs on {npc} and an abacus. Every winter {he} goes through the accounts of the estates by lamplight, finding out what the stewards have stolen. This year {he} sets a second abacus in front of you and says it is time you learned how rich people get poor.

mem.note: checked the grain figures with me

effects.log: Three estates, and one of them has been sending the same harvest for six years. {npc} is delighted, and writes a name down.

choices.text: Ask why the house does not hire someone

mem.note: asked why we do not hire someone

effects.log: {npc} shows you the last person the house hired, on the page where the name stops appearing. You pick up the abacus.

events.text: The name {npc} wrote down has come in person, with gifts, and is waiting in the outer hall. An old steward, with grandchildren. {npc} asks you what ought to be done. {He} is not really asking about the steward.

choices.text: Have it paid back, and let the steward stay

mem.note: chose mercy with the accounts open

effects.log: The old steward weeps, and repays it, and steals nothing for eleven years. {npc} says that is about what you can expect.

choices.text: Send the steward away, and let everyone hear why

effects.log: The other stewards' figures are very neat that spring. {npc} says it has its uses, and that you will think about it sometimes.

events.text: {npc}'s eyes are not what they were, and {he} has quietly begun passing you the small columns. Tonight {he} falls asleep at the table, with the beads under {his} hand, in the middle of the estates of the east.

choices.text: Finish the east, and put the lamp out

mem.note: finished the east while I slept

effects.log: In the morning the book is done, in a hand almost the same as the one above it. {npc} reads it, changes one figure, and says nothing else.

choices.text: Put a quilt over {him}, and leave it

effects.log: {He} finishes it the next night, and pretends nothing happened. The quilt is back on your bed by morning, folded.

events.text: Once a year the tenants of the house come up to the gate with what they owe, and every year the family sends its least important member to sit at the table and receive them. That has been {npc} for a long time. {He} knows all their names. {He} asks if you would like to see what your rice looks like.

choices.text: Sit beside {him}, and write the tallies

effects.log: By noon your hand aches. An old woman tells you that you have your great-grandmother's nose, and that it never did anyone any good.

choices.text: Go down the line, and ask about the harvest

mem.note: went down the line and asked

effects.log: They are very polite. {npc} tells you afterward which of them were lying to you, and why they had to.

events.text: A bad year, and half the line has come up with empty hands, and they have not come to beg: they stand at the gate and say nothing. {npc} has the steward's instructions in {his} sleeve and has not taken them out. {He} looks at you.

choices.text: Forgive a third of it, and answer for it to the elders (10 taels)

mem.note: answered for it to the elders

effects.log: The elders have a great deal to say. The line goes home. Next year it comes back, and it remembers.

choices.text: Hold to the tally, and open the old granary as a loan

mem.note: opened the granary as a loan

effects.log: Nobody starves and nobody is grateful. {npc} says that is how you can tell it was done properly.

events.text: {npc} is too old to sit at the table all day. {He} has come anyway, on a chair with a cushion, to tell you that the house has decided it is you now, since you have grown so good at it. {He} says that nobody is ever thanked for this, and that it is the best seat there is.

effects.log: You know their names by the third year, and their children's. Some of them come up early, to tell you things the steward does not.

choices.text: Find a young cousin, and teach them how

effects.log: The cousin is terrified. {npc} spends the whole day on the cushion, correcting both of you, and has never been happier.

events.arc: The Cup at the Clan Feast
events.text: At the clan feast there is a custom that the young of the house must each drink to the elders, in order, three hundred people watching, without spilling. {npc} is next, and is shaking so hard that the cup is ringing against {his} ring, and asks you to stand beside {him} and be looked at instead.

effects.log: The hall gasps, and an elder has to be fanned. Nobody at all notices how {npc} manages.

choices.text: Stand close, and say something rude under your breath

mem.note: made me laugh instead of shake

effects.log: {npc} is trying so hard not to laugh that {his} hands go perfectly steady. It is a very dignified toast.

events.arc: The Cup at the Clan Feast
events.text: {npc} has been told who {he} is to marry, for the good of the house. It is a fair match and a decent person. {He} has come to the old training yard after dark, in {his} good clothes, and {he} is not there to ask you for anything. {He} only did not want to be anywhere with a roof.

choices.text: Spar, until neither of you can stand

effects.log: You ruin the good clothes. Nothing is said, and in the morning {npc} goes in to breakfast with {his} head up.

mem.note: sat on the wall with me

effects.log: You sit there until the watch changes. At some point {he} says it could be worse. You agree that it could.

events.arc: The Cup at the Clan Feast
events.text: The clan feast again. A very small child of the house is next in line with the cup, and it is ringing. {npc} catches your eye across three hundred people, and very slowly tips {his} own cup until it starts to pour.

effects.log: It is talked about for years. The custom is, in the end, quietly changed, and everyone claims to have wanted that all along.

choices.text: Go and stand beside the child

mem.note: went and stood beside the child

effects.log: You say something rude under your breath. The child looks up at you with enormous eyes, and the cup goes perfectly steady.

events.text: The founder's sword hangs in the great hall, and nobody but the head of the house may lay a hand on it. You once took the blame when {npc} was found polishing it at midnight. Today {he} wakes you before dawn and leads you down there by the sleeve, as if you were both still in trouble. {He} wants to repay you. {He} has brought the polish.

effects.log: It is lighter than it looks, {npc} says, and much worse made. Three hundred years of awe, and the balance is terrible.
You have never touched it before. There is a nick near the hilt that is in none of the stories, and {npc} tells you who put it there.

events.text: There is a ceremony, and the sword is to be carried in procession, and the steward has just noticed that it is much cleaner than it ought to be. Inquiries are being made. {npc} sits across from you at breakfast with an expression of complete innocence.

effects.log: The steward questions eleven servants and a cat. Nobody ever finds out. {npc} passes you the pickles, gravely.

choices.text: Say you did it, before anyone else is blamed

effects.log: You get a very long lecture, and nobody else gets anything. {npc} pays for your supper that night, as is now traditional.

events.text: {npc} cannot manage the stairs to the hall at night now. {He} gives you the little pot of polish, nearly empty and forty years old, and says the sword will want doing at the next new moon. {He} says somebody ought to know where the nick is.

choices.text: Go down at the new moon

mem.note: goes down at the new moon

effects.log: It is very quiet down there without {him}. You tell {him} about it in the morning, and {he} corrects your technique.

mem.note: carried me down one last time

effects.log: {He} weighs less than the sword looks. {He} does the nick {him}self and will not let you help.

events.text: {npc} came to this house at seventeen with a chest of red silk, and has never been seen to open it. You stood by {him} once, in front of the elders, when it cost you. Tonight {he} has it carried to your rooms, and sits down on the lid, and asks if you would like to know who {he} was before all this.

choices.text: Say yes, and sit down too

effects.log: It takes until the lamp fails. There was a river, and a boy with a bad singing voice, and a very good shot with a bow, and that was {npc}. You had no idea.
{He} lifts the lid. It is not silk underneath the top layer. It is a bow, unstrung, kept oiled for thirty years.

events.text: An inspection of the inner court is coming, and {npc} wants the bow out of the house before the elders' wives come through counting things. {He} has a plan. It requires you, a laundry basket, and a straight face.

mem.note: carried the basket past the elders

effects.log: You meet an elder on the stairs and discuss the weather for some time. {npc} watches from a window and is enjoying this far too much.

choices.text: Say it should stay, and that {he} should stand behind it

mem.note: told me to stand behind it

effects.log: {npc} thinks about that for a whole day. The inspectors find the bow hanging on the wall, and {npc} beside it, and nobody writes anything down.

events.text: {npc} wants to see if {he} can still do it. There is a target at the end of the back garden, at dawn, with nobody about. Thirty-eight years. {He} strings the bow on the second try, and holds out three arrows for you to count.

effects.log: The first goes wide. The second goes wide. The third stands in the middle, humming. {npc} unstrings the bow and goes in to breakfast.
You are dreadful. {npc} has not been so happy in this house since the day {he} came to it.

events.text: The house's tutors set a thousand lines for every small offence, and for one whole winter you copied {npc}'s as well as your own. {npc} has not forgotten. Today {he} arrives with a thousand lines in your handwriting, which {he} has taught {him}self to forge, in case you should ever need them.

effects.log: You will need them by the spring. It is a little frightening how good they are.

choices.text: Ask what else {he} has learned to forge

mem.note: asked what else I can forge

effects.log: {npc} looks over each shoulder, and tells you. You make {him} promise a number of things.

events.text: A letter has gone out in the name of an elder, cancelling a very dull inspection. The elder is puzzled. The hand is perfect. {npc} is reading a book in the courtyard, upside down, and does not look up when you come and stand over {him}.

choices.text: Turn the book the right way up, and walk on

mem.note: turned my book the right way up

effects.log: You say nothing to anyone. The inspection is put off till autumn, and the whole younger branch breathes out.

choices.text: Make {him} write the elder a real apology

effects.log: It is the finest apology that elder has ever had, and it is in the elder's own hand. {npc} really cannot help it.

events.text: {npc} has been offered a post writing the house's letters, the ones that go to governors and courts. It is a great honour. Nobody on that council knows why {he} is so good at matching every hand in the province. {He} has come to ask if you are going to tell them.

choices.text: Say it is the safest place for {him}

mem.note: knows what I am and got me the post

effects.log: {npc} takes the post. The house's letters have never been so persuasive, and you have someone to ask.

choices.text: Say you will have to tell them, and go with {him}

mem.note: stood by me when I told them

effects.log: There is a terrible silence. Then the oldest elder asks whether {npc} can do the Governor's hand, and things go on from there.

events.text: {npc} is left off the guest lists of this house, for reasons that are told in low voices. Once, when you were young, you wrote {him} a letter when nobody else would. Today {he} turns up at the side gate in a coat that has been somewhere, with a very small, very rude carved monkey, and says it is the only thing {he} has ever been proud of owning.

mem.note: brought me in by the front

effects.log: Eleven relations remember appointments. {npc} eats two dinners and tells a story about a governor that you are still thinking about.

choices.text: Sit with {him} on the step, and hear where {he} has been

mem.note: sat on the step and listened

effects.log: Nine provinces, three wives of other people, and a boat. It is the most you have ever learned about the world in one sitting.

events.text: The elders have heard that {npc} has been seen near the house again, and want it stopped. There is an allowance they could cut. It is not large. It is, you learn, all {he} has, and {he} has never once asked for more.

effects.log: {npc} sends a note that says only: I know. Another monkey arrives, ruder than the first.

choices.text: Go to the elders and argue it

effects.log: You lose, twice, and win the third time, largely because they are tired. One of them asks you, later, whether the story about the governor is true.

events.text: A cart at the side gate, and {npc} on it, a good deal thinner. {He} has come to ask a thing {he} has never asked: whether there is a corner of the ancestral hall where a person like {him} might have a very small tablet, when the time comes.

choices.text: Promise it, and see it done

effects.log: It is a very small tablet, and it took you a year of arguing. Somebody keeps leaving a carved monkey in front of it. It is not you.

choices.text: Bring {him} inside now, and let the elders object

effects.log: They object. {npc} takes the good room over the garden, and tells the young cousins about the boat.

events.text: {npc} keeps the house's list of suitable persons: who may marry whom, which branch owes which, whose grandfather was not as described. It runs to nine volumes. A cousin's match has come apart, and {npc} needs someone to read out names while {he} crosses them through.

effects.log: You learn more about the great houses in an afternoon than in ten years of lessons. Very little of it is fit to repeat.

choices.text: Ask to see your own page

mem.note: asked to see their own page

effects.log: {npc} shuts the book on your finger, not hard, and says you will see it when it is finished. It is apparently quite long.

events.text: The cousin is in love with someone who is in none of the nine volumes. {npc} has found out, and has not yet told anyone. {He} has the pen in {his} hand and the book open at the back, and is looking at you. Nobody has ever been written in by hand who was not born to it.

effects.log: {npc} invents a grandfather, a very dull one. It is the finest thing in the nine volumes, and nobody ever checks.

choices.text: Say the list is the list

mem.note: said the list is the list

effects.log: {npc} nods, and shuts the book. The cousin marries well. You see the cousin at a banquet, years later, and neither of you says anything.

events.text: {npc} has decided to burn volume four. It concerns a generation now dead and nothing in it has ever done anyone any good. {He} has carried it down to the kitchen stove {him}self and is waiting, with some ceremony, for a second pair of hands.

choices.text: Feed it in, page by page

mem.note: burned the fourth volume with me

effects.log: It takes all night. {npc} reads out the best of it first. You have never laughed so much or felt so strange.
{npc} looks at the page you chose, and at you, and slides it into your sleeve, and says that person is still alive, as it happens.

events.arc: The Call on the Other House
events.text: Once a year {npc} pays a call on the matriarch of the rival house, and they drink one cup of tea, and say nothing true for two hours. They have done this for fifty years. Today {npc} wants a young person to carry the gift and to sit very straight, and to watch what the other one does with {his} left hand.

effects.log: Afterward {npc} asks you what the tea meant, and the second biscuit, and the remark about the weather. You had not known it was a battle. You know now.

mem.note: said something honest in that room

effects.log: A silence falls. The old enemy looks at you with sudden interest, and {npc} pinches you hard, all the way home, and is delighted.

events.arc: The Call on the Other House
events.text: Word has come that the old enemy is ill. {npc} has had the good tea packed, and then unpacked it. {He} is sitting in {his} rooms with {his} hands folded. Fifty years, and {he} does not know what is allowed. {He} asks, very sharply, why you are standing there.

choices.text: Say you will carry the tea

mem.note: carried the tea to the sick room

effects.log: They sit for an hour. Nobody says anything true. On the way home {npc} is very quiet, and holds your arm on the stairs.

choices.text: Offer to send a physician, in the house's name

mem.note: sent a physician in the house's name

effects.log: It is the correct thing. The other house sends the correct thanks. {npc} looks out of the window for the rest of the day.

events.arc: The Call on the Other House
events.text: The old enemy has died, and a parcel has come for {npc} from the other house: one biscuit, on a very good plate, with no note. {npc} has looked at it since morning. {He} says you must help {him} decide what it means.

effects.log: {npc} snorts. {He} eats it, slowly, all of it, and sends back the plate with one biscuit on it. There is nobody there to receive it.

choices.text: Say it means {he} is the only one left who would know

effects.log: {npc} does not answer. {He} keeps the plate on {his} table for as long as {he} lives, and nobody is allowed to dust it.

events.arc: The Petitioners at the Side Gate
events.text: The front gate of this house is for guests. The side gate, on the first of the month, is for anyone with a grievance, and there are always more of them than the stewards admit. {npc} goes down to sit there, in a plain coat, against all advice. Today {he} says you should come and hear what your name means to people.

effects.log: A drowned field, a stolen daughter's dowry, a boundary stone moved by a steward of this house. {npc} writes each one down, and tells you nothing will be easy.
Nobody knows who you are, until someone does. After that they will not take the water, and you learn something from that as well.

events.arc: The Petitioners at the Side Gate
events.text: One of the petitions is about a steward of the house, and it is true, and that steward is related to an elder. {npc} has the paper in {his} hand. {He} wants to know what you would do, since it will be you one day. {He} has not decided either.

choices.text: Move the steward, and pay the farmer quietly (5 taels)

effects.log: It costs less than a feud. The field goes back. The elder sends you a very pleasant note.

choices.text: Bring it before the whole council

effects.log: It is a long and ugly month. The side gate is much more crowded afterward. {npc} says that is how you know.

events.arc: The Petitioners at the Side Gate
events.text: {npc} is too frail for the bench at the side gate, and the stewards have been saying, kindly, that it might be time to let the custom lapse. There are forty people out there this morning. {He} looks at the plain coat on its peg, and then at you.

effects.log: It does not fit. You sit there till dark. It is noticed, the way such things are noticed in a province.

mem.note: carried me down to the gate

effects.log: {He} sleeps through most of the afternoon, with {his} hand on the list. Nobody in the line says anything about it.

events.text: There are nineteen guards on the walls of this house, and a place behind the old kitchen where none of them can be bothered to look. {npc} has found it. {He} has a plain coat for each of you, a pocket of coppers, and a very strong wish to eat something from a stall, standing up, like a person.

mem.note: went over the wall with me

effects.log: Fried dough, in the rain. It is the best thing you have ever eaten. A guard waves at you on the way back in, and you never find out why.
You sit on the wall for two hours with your heart going. {npc} comes back with a bag of something for you, and it is still warm.

events.text: Nobody in the town knows who {npc} is. There is a stall-keeper's child {he} has been talking to, and a fair, and it has been a month of evenings. Now the house has begun to talk about matches. {npc} sits on the wall in the plain coat, and does not go down either side.

mem.note: sat on the wall and said nothing

effects.log: The watch changes. Fried dough can be smelled from here, if the wind is right. Neither of you mentions it.

choices.text: Say {he} should tell them who {he} is

mem.note: told me to say who I am

effects.log: {npc} tells them. It does not go as {he} hoped, or as you feared. {He} comes back over the wall a little older, and eats alone for a while.

events.text: The back wall has been rebuilt, by order, and is very high. {npc} is grown and has a seat on the council and a great many people who stand up when {he} comes in. {He} has sent you a note: there is a gap behind the new granary. {He} has brought the coats.

effects.log: It is harder than it was. The stall is run by someone's grandchild now. It is just as good, and nobody at all looks up.

choices.text: Send a plate of fried dough to the council chamber

mem.note: sent fried dough to the council

effects.log: It arrives during a discussion of grain tariffs. {npc} does not look up, but {he} moves the plate to where {he} can reach it.

events.arc: The Old One in the Back Palace
events.text: Everyone who enters your presence now does it on their knees, and has rehearsed what to say. Not {npc}, who lives at the back of the palace among the cabbages {he} has insisted on planting, and sends a eunuch with the message that the throne is to come and hold a basket, if it is not too busy.

effects.log: Four ministers wait in the corridor all afternoon. Nobody calls you anything for three hours. You have forgotten what that was like.

choices.text: Send for {him} to come to the hall

mem.note: sent for me like a minister

effects.log: {npc} comes, walks the whole length of the hall, does not kneel, looks at you, and goes back to the cabbages. It is reported in three provinces.

events.arc: The Old One in the Back Palace
events.text: The censors have complained about the cabbages. They spoil the line of the back gardens, and a former person of rank ought not to be seen with mud on {him}. {npc} has read the memorial, and has used it to tie up some beans.

choices.text: Write across it, leave the old fool alone

effects.log: It is copied and passed from hand to hand in the ministries. Nobody files another. {npc} says the handwriting has got worse.

choices.text: Go and tie up beans for an afternoon, where the censors can see

mem.note: tied the beans where they could see

effects.log: Nobody knows what the rule is for this. A censor is seen standing very still at a window.

events.arc: The Old One in the Back Palace
events.text: {npc} sends for you, and this time there is no basket. {He} is in {his} chair, among the last of the cabbages, and wants to tell you one thing that has never been written down about the person who sat in your seat before. Then {he} says you are not to answer. You are only to go on planting something.

choices.text: Plant something, with your own hands

mem.note: planted something with their own hands

effects.log: It is a very poor row. The gardeners are forbidden to straighten it, and it comes up crooked for as long as you reign.
You hold up the whole business of the realm for one evening. Nothing falls down. You will think about that.

events.text: You head the clan now, and {npc}, who held your hand at your first festival, addresses you by title, bows at the right depth, and has asked for an hour of your time. {He} keeps the clan register. A family at the far end of the valley have asked to be entered, on the grounds of a great-grandfather nobody can prove.

mem.note: looked at the proof with me

effects.log: There is one letter and a very good story. {npc} clearly wants you to say no, and just as clearly wants you to have read it first.
{npc} straightens up, one joint at a time. In here, {he} says, and only in here. {He} calls you what {he} called you when you were six.

events.text: The far-valley family has come in person, thirty of them, with their one letter, and their children in their best clothes. The elders do not want them. The clan is short of young people who can hold a sword. {npc} brings you the register and the brush, and steps back.

effects.log: The elders are displeased for a decade. Thirty people bow very low, and the youngest of them can really fight.

choices.text: Refuse, with a gift for the road

mem.note: sent them away with a gift

effects.log: The register stays clean. {npc} rules the line under that year very straight, and has nothing to say about it.

events.text: {npc} wants to show you something in the oldest volume. Your own great-great-grandfather's entry has been written over. Under the good ink, if you hold it to the lamp, there is a different name, a far-valley sort of name. {He} has known for forty years, and has never bowed any less.

choices.text: Close the book, and pour the wine

mem.note: closed the book and poured the wine

effects.log: Neither of you ever mentions it again. You do notice that you have begun looking at the register a little differently.

choices.text: Ask what else is under there

mem.note: asked what else is under there

effects.log: {npc} smiles for the first time since you took the seat. {He} has been waiting for someone to ask. It takes the whole winter.

events.text: The family's patent of nobility, with the old Emperor's seal, is kept in a box which {npc} airs on the first dry day of every autumn. You helped {him} carry it down once, when everyone else had forgotten. This year {he} unrolls it on the terrace for you, and shows you that the third line was very clearly written in by someone else.

effects.log: A clever clerk, {npc} says, two hundred years ago, for a very reasonable fee. All nobility begins with somebody knowing a clerk.

choices.text: Say nothing, and hold down the corner

effects.log: There is a breeze. {npc} watches you hold it with both hands, and seems satisfied with something.

events.text: A cousin has been boasting at court about the family's antiquity, and someone at court has begun to ask to see the patent. {npc} is on the terrace with the box and a candle. {He} wishes to discuss, purely as a question of history, what happens to old paper in a fire.

effects.log: The patent goes to court, third line and all. The clerk was very good. Nobody notices a thing, and {npc} is almost disappointed.

choices.text: Have a word with the cousin, instead

effects.log: The cousin stops boasting, and develops an interest in fishing. {npc} blows out the candle and looks at you with new respect.

events.text: {npc} has found the clerk's great-great-grandchildren, who keep a small and failing shop in the lower town and have no idea. {He} thinks something is owed. {He} has put on {his} oldest coat, to go and buy a great many brushes that nobody needs.

choices.text: Go along, and buy ink as well (3 taels)

effects.log: The shop does very well that year. {npc} tells them nothing. {He} has the brushes sent to the house, and there are enough to last until the dynasty falls.

choices.text: Say the debt is two hundred years old

effects.log: {npc} says that is exactly how old a debt has to be, and goes alone. You find one good brush on your desk the next morning.

events.text: The line of your house is painted on the wall of the long gallery, every head of it, and when you took the seat the painter added you at the bottom. {npc} has walked down to look, on two sticks. {He} says the painter has left you room for about four more generations, which is either very hopeful or very rude.

choices.text: Ask how long the wall is

mem.note: asked how long the wall is

effects.log: {npc} has you walk it. There is a stretch of bare plaster at the far end, and {he} tells you what happened to the last house that ran out of wall.

choices.text: Stand beside your own name a while

effects.log: It is a very small name, in a very long line. {npc} pats your arm, and tells you that they all looked like that at first.

events.text: There is a name on the wall that was painted over, with some care, in the time of your great-grandparents. {npc} remembers that person. {He} is the last who does. {He} would like, before it is too late, to tell somebody what that head of the house was really like.

effects.log: The elders are appalled. The house does not fall down. {npc} walks down on {his} sticks to see it, and stays there most of the day.

choices.text: Hear all of it, and leave the wall alone

effects.log: You know something now that the wall does not. {npc} says that this is what heads of the house are for.

events.text: {npc} wants a small thing done. Next to the line there is a blank space on the wall. {He} would like a few words there about the people who kept this house running and are on no list of any kind: the cooks, the second sons, a clever maid. {He} has the names. {He} is afraid {he} is the last who has them.

effects.log: It takes a painter a month, and it looks very odd. Visitors stop there longer than at the rest of the line.

choices.text: Write them down in the family book, where they will be safe

effects.log: Forty names, and what each one could do. {npc} makes you read it back to {him} twice, and corrects the cook's.

events.arc: The Chess Under the Locust Tree
events.text: There is a stone stool in your courtyard now. The old men under the locust tree gave it up as a wedding gift, grumbling. {npc} sets out the pieces every afternoon and waits for you to come home and think.

mem.note: sets out the board for me too

effects.log: You lose, late. {npc} pours the tea and sets up the board again at once.

choices.text: Call the moves with your eyes shut

mem.note: played blind with me, for the fun of it

effects.log: You both forget whose side is whose. The neighbours can hear the laughing from the lane.

events.text: There is split bamboo on your table and fish glue on your good bowl. The stall went to someone else, but over your bed a paper swallow turns on a thread, and {npc} has started on a second one. {He} says a house should have something in it that wants to leave and does not.

choices.text: Hold the wing while the glue sets

effects.log: You hold it for an hour. It is a sort of duck. {npc} hangs it beside the swallow anyway.

choices.text: Take it out to the bridge at dusk

mem.note: ran with the kite for me

effects.log: It flies. {npc} shouts instructions from the bridge, waving, as if you had never met.

events.text: On the first of each month {npc} still gets up before light and takes two brooms from behind your door. The temple has other sweepers now. {He} has never said you must come. {He} only leaves the second broom leaning where you will see it.

choices.text: Go with {him}, a hundred and eight steps

mem.note: still comes to sweep with me

effects.log: One leaf at a time. By the top, neither of you has anything left to say, and it is the best talk of the month.

choices.text: Sweep your own courtyard while {he} is gone

mem.note: had the yard swept when I came home

effects.log: {npc} comes home and looks at the yard for a while. {He} tells you which leaves you missed.
