events.text: {npc} has no need to go down to the washing stones now. But on wash days you hear it from the back of the house, over a basin: the song for washing, the one with no name. The whole house goes quiet to listen. When {he} stops, everyone carries on.

mem.note: still sings the next verse back

effects.log: You get it nearly right. {npc} sings the next one at you, over the basin, very fond and a little rude.

choices.text: Stand in the doorway and listen

mem.note: stopped in the doorway to listen

effects.log: {npc} knows you are there. {He} sings the last verse a little slower, and does not look up.

events.text: {npc} brought the old ledger along, and it sits on the shelf with the household accounts. Looking for something else, you find your own page. Under what {he} wrote that first day there is a new line in {his} square hand: crossed over, and stayed.

choices.text: Add a line of your own

effects.log: You write: owes nothing, is owed everything. {npc} corrects your spelling, and leaves the rest.

choices.text: Say nothing, and put it back

mem.note: found the page and let me keep it

effects.log: {npc} sees the ledger is an inch out of place, and smiles at the wall for most of the morning.

events.text: Every morning {npc} walks a songbird through your courtyard, three times round, the cage swinging. Every morning {he} stops by your door and asks if you have heard a bird sing like this one. You have. You heard it yesterday.

effects.log: {npc} tells you the bird's whole family history again. It has grown since last time.
The bird answers you. {npc} is amazed and somewhat jealous, as {he} is every time.

events.arc: The Tea Stall at the Crossroads
events.text: The kettle came along with {npc}, and there is a bench by your gate that nobody asked for. Strangers sit on it. {He} pours for them without asking and talks about the weather in four directions. On a nail in the kitchen hangs a cup with your name scratched on it, so you will know which one is yours.

choices.text: Sit on the bench with the strangers

effects.log: The tea is bitter and good. A carter tells you that you are lucky to live near such a place.

choices.text: Mend the bench before it goes

effects.log: It is too comfortable now. {npc} says people will never leave, and is pleased.

events.text: There is good timber stacked in your yard, and {npc} has been seen measuring your gate. {He} measures it twice. Asked what for, {he} says it is nothing, and that the wall on that side was never very good anyway.

choices.text: Ask how big it is going to be

effects.log: {npc} draws it in the dirt with a stick. It will fit through the gate. {He} seems almost sorry.

choices.text: Take the wall down now, to save time

mem.note: took the wall down for me

effects.log: You are both still laughing when the neighbours come to see what fell. The barn on the river is not the only place with a missing wall now.

events.arc: The Poems on the Tavern Wall
events.text: One wall of your house has never been painted, by order. {npc} writes on it with whatever is to hand: the wine, the weather, you. On New Year's Eve {he} reads it all aloud, terribly, and every guest applauds. You are still not sure it is the poems.

effects.log: It does not scan. {npc} reads it aloud and makes it worse, and better.
{npc} reads the whole wall to you by lamplight. There is one in the corner about a goat. {He} will not discuss it.

events.text: In the dark {npc} finds the knot in your shoulder without asking, the way {he} found it the first day. {His} thumbs stop on it. What have you been carrying now, {he} says, and waits. {He} has all night, and {he} has never once needed you to look well.

effects.log: You talk. {npc} works the knot out as you talk. You sleep better than you have in a year.
{npc} laughs and says a sword sits lower than that. The knot goes anyway.

events.arc: Eleven Cats at the End of the Lane
events.text: The cats came with the marriage. They have walked your whole house, room by room, and taken the bed, the stove and the good cushion. {npc} says they have voted on you and it was close. The large orange one has moved onto your chest and is, {he} tells you, the deciding vote.

choices.text: Lie still, and let it stand

effects.log: You lose the feeling in one arm. {npc} looks very relieved. The cat looks very calm.

mem.note: learned the names of my cats

effects.log: {npc} tests you at supper. You get ten. The eleventh looks at you from the rafters and does not forgive it.

events.arc: The Old Soldier on the Wall
events.text: There are two stools on the roof of your house, facing north. {npc} still goes up in the evening, from habit, and looks at the road a while. Tonight, when you climb up, {he} looks at you instead, and says the road can watch itself for an hour.

effects.log: Nobody comes up the north road. It is peaceful. Neither of you goes down until the stars are out.
{npc} drinks it without a word. The next evening there is a little table up there as well.

events.text: Every night {npc} tells you the next part of a story. {He} has been telling it since the wedding, and it has gone on longer than any you ever heard in the market. You have asked how it ends. {He} says you of all people should understand the business.

choices.text: Say what you think happens next

mem.note: tells the next part with me

effects.log: {npc} considers it, makes a face, and tells a better one. You recognise half of it.

choices.text: Fall asleep in the middle, as you always do

effects.log: {npc} goes on for a while anyway, more quietly. In the morning {he} starts from just before you dropped off.

events.text: {npc} has hung a small red jacket on a peg by your door. {His} child outgrew it long ago. {He} says it stays there for the day anyone in this house gets lost, so they will know what to look for. You have stopped asking who {he} means.

choices.text: Touch the sleeve on your way out

mem.note: touches the jacket on the way out

effects.log: It is a small habit. {npc} has seen you do it, and has never said so.
{npc} eats the head first, gravely, and says you know the rules of this house.

events.text: Nothing in this house gets thrown away. Every cracked bowl goes into a basket by the stove, and bit by bit the kitchen floor is turning into something. By the door there is already a small mule, looking determined. {npc} says nothing here is ever broken, only early.

mem.note: broke a good dish for my floor

effects.log: {npc} looks at the pieces, and at you, and says it was the right dish.

choices.text: Kneel down and set the next piece

mem.note: set a piece in the floor

effects.log: It goes in crooked. {npc} leaves it crooked. It is the part guests ask about.

events.text: You smell it before you wake: {npc} bakes before light, from a lifetime of habit. There is always one bun over, set out on the sill by the lane. Some mornings it is gone by breakfast. {npc} has never once looked to see who takes it.

effects.log: Now there are two on the sill. By the end of the year there are five, and the lane is fatter.

mem.note: ate three, which is the highest praise

effects.log: {npc} understands. {He} always did.

events.text: {npc} still wakes at the third hour. {He} walks the house in the dark without a rattle, gate, yard, kitchen, and comes back to your door. All is well, {he} says, very quietly, to nobody. Then {he} goes back to bed. {He} thinks you sleep through it.

choices.text: Say, the fourth hour, all is well

effects.log: There is a silence, and then a laugh into the pillow. A cat disagrees from somewhere in the yard.

choices.text: Stay asleep, as far as {npc} knows

mem.note: lets me think they sleep through it

effects.log: You lie still and listen to the footsteps. It is a good house to be watched over in.

events.text: Every year, on the day you first met, {npc} writes out a poem in {his} best hand and lays it by your bowl. {He} calls it the interest. You have asked what it is the interest on, and {he} says that is not the sort of debt one reads about in books.

effects.log: Your poem is very bad. {npc} frames it, and hangs it where visitors have to pass.
{npc} refuses. The rate, {he} informs you, has just gone up.

events.text: On wash days {npc} still ties {his} ring to the paddle, for safe keeping, in a house where nothing is going to float away. You have mentioned that this is how {he} lost it. {He} says that is how {he} found you, and goes on tying the knot.

effects.log: It is a bad knot. {npc} leaves it. It holds for years, out of what looks like spite.
There are no ducks on your stream, and then there are. {npc} calls you a philosopher, and means it, a bit.

events.text: A red bucket hangs beside your door now, with a chipped teacup sitting in it. {npc} checks both every evening before bed: water in the one, nothing in the other. {He} says a house should be ready. {He} has never told you what for, and it is not about fire any more.

effects.log: {npc} checks it anyway, then looks up and nods, the way one watchman nods at another.

choices.text: Ask for your tea in the old cup

effects.log: {npc} is outraged, and then proud. You drink it on the step.

events.text: You find it under your bowl: a letter, sealed, addressed in a post rider's hand, from the next room. {npc} has written you one a month since the wedding. They say what the weather was. They say what was for dinner, which you ate. {He} says some letters ought to get there on the first try.

choices.text: Write back, and leave it under the other bowl

effects.log: {npc} reads it standing, and then carries it about in {his} sleeve for a week.

choices.text: Keep them all in a box

effects.log: There are forty now. {npc} has seen the box, and pretends otherwise.

events.text: You have not had a loose button since the wedding. Your old coats have come back from the dark of the chest looking younger than you. In the evenings {npc} holds a needle out without looking up, and you thread it, and neither of you says anything, and it is the best hour of the day.

effects.log: A hundred needles in a pin cushion. {npc} says it will last the week, and looks at you until you sit down again.

choices.text: Wear the good robe to market, for no reason

mem.note: wore my robe for no reason

effects.log: Everyone asks who made it. You give them the name, and watch them work out where you heard it.
